NASHR:v1p469/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p469/r5.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p469/r5.claim: The four faces also apply to taftaʾu, atawakkaʾu, and similar forms written with waw; a fifth face substitutes alif by regular softening, while a written alif allows alif substitution or eased rūm.
NASHR:v1p469/r5.anchor: وكذلك تجري هذه الأربعة في (تفتؤ، واتوكؤا)

THALABI:v6p242/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p242/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p242/r1.claim: Moses used the staff to shake leaves from trees for his sheep to eat.
THALABI:v6p242/r1.anchor: وأهش وأخبط بها الشجر ليتناثر ورقها فتأكل غنمي

THALABI:v6p242/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p242/r2.speaker: النضر بن شميل
THALABI:v6p242/r2.claim: Al-Nadr ibn Shumayl recounts al-Khalil’s explanation that Arabic often substitutes sīn for shīn, as in examples for sneezing, armor, and a seal.
THALABI:v6p242/r2.anchor: وقال النضر بن شميل: سألت الخليل عن قراءة عكرمة فقال: العرب تعاقب بين الشين والسين

THALABI:v6p242/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p242/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v6p242/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says Moses’ staff carried food and water, produced them, herded and guarded sheep, fought attackers, drew water from wells, lit his way at night, and grew fruit trees on demand.
THALABI:v6p242/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس: كان موسى عليه السلام يحمل عليها زاده وسقاءه

THALABI:v6p242/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p242/r7.speaker: عكرمة
THALABI:v6p242/r7.claim: Ikrima reads وأهس with sīn, meaning ‘I drive away the sheep’; Arabic often alternates sīn and shīn.
THALABI:v6p242/r7.anchor: وقرأ عكرمة «وأهس» بالسين يعني وازجر بها الغنم

THALABI:v6p242/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p242/r8.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p242/r8.claim: مآرب means needs or uses; its singular has two vowel forms, and the plural أخر is avoided to preserve the verse endings.
THALABI:v6p242/r8.anchor: ولي فيها مآرب حوائج ومنافع، واحدتها مأربة ومأربة بفتح الراء وضمها أخرى

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p21/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p21/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p21/r6.claim: The common meaning of the verb is bringing down leaves from a tree.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p21/r6.anchor: means to bring down leaves from a tree.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p21/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p21/r7.speaker: ‘Ukbar ī
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p21/r7.claim: ‘Ukbarī reads Moses’ phrase as meaning that he protects and tends his herd with the staff.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p21/r7.anchor: ‘Ukbar ī is of the opinion that the words

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p21/r8.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p21/r8.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p21/r8.claim: Islahi follows the common meaning because ‘Ukbarī supplied no linguistic evidence for his alternative.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p21/r8.anchor: So I have followed its common meaning in this regard.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p21/r9.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p21/r9.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p21/r9.claim: Moses elaborated because he understood the question as affectionate and wanted the exchange to continue.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p21/r9.anchor: he fully understood that the question posed was not merely an inquiry, it carried a great amount of affection in it.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p21/r10.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p21/r10.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p21/r10.claim: Extending conversation with someone deeply loved is a natural desire.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p21/r10.anchor: prolonging the conversation with him is a natural desire.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p307/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p307/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p307/r8.claim: Tawakkaʾa and itta kaʾa mean leaning; the related word muttakaʾ was discussed in Joseph. Hashsha for sheep shakes down leaves; for a person it means cheerfulness.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p307/r8.anchor: وتقدمت هذه المادة في سورة يوسف في قوله متكأ وشرحت هنا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p307/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p307/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p307/r9.claim: Ghanam is a feminine collective; maʾriba and irba mean need, while ḥayya covers snakes of any sex or size.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p307/r9.anchor: الغنم معروف وهو اسم جنس مؤنث. المأربة بضم الراء وفتحها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p321/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p321/r1.speaker: ابن أبي إسحاق والجحدري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p321/r1.claim: Ibn Abī Isḥāq and al-Jaḥdarī read عصي, replacing the alif with yāʾ and assimilating it to the first-person yāʾ.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p321/r1.anchor: وقرأ ابن أبي إسحاق والجحدري عصي بقلب الألف ياء وإدغامها في ياء المتكلم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p321/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p321/r2.speaker: الحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p321/r2.claim: Al-Ḥasan reads عصاي with kasra on the yāʾ, also transmitted from Ibn Abī Isḥāq and Abū ʿAmr; the kasra resolves two adjacent quiescent letters.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p321/r2.anchor: وقرأ الحسن عصاي بكسر الياء وهي مروية عن ابن أبي إسحاق

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p321/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p321/r3.speaker: أبو إسحاق والجحدري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p321/r3.claim: Abū Isḥāq and al-Jaḥdarī are also reported to read عصاي with a quiescent yāʾ.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p321/r3.anchor: وعن أبي إسحاق والجحدري عصاي بسكون الياء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p321/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p321/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p321/r4.claim: أتوكؤا means leaning on the staff while walking or standing; Moses adds useful detail beyond the direct answer, as in Prophetic answers that add a benefit.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p321/r4.anchor: أتوكؤا عليها أي أتحامل عليها في المشي والوقوف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p321/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p321/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p321/r5.claim: The added detail reflects Moses’ desire to prolong intimate conversation with God and its delight, gratitude for the staff’s benefits, and a move from two specific uses to general purposes.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p321/r5.anchor: وحكمة زيادة موسى عليه السلام رغبته في مطاولة مناجاته

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p321/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p321/r6.speaker: الشاعر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p321/r6.claim: The poet wishes to prolong reproach because its conversation is pleasurable, illustrating Moses’ desire to extend his colloquy.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p321/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p321/r7.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p321/r7.claim: One view makes أتوكؤا an answer to a second, unstated question about what Moses does with the staff.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p321/r7.anchor: وقيل: أتوكؤا عليها جواب لسؤال آخر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p321/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p321/r8.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p321/r8.claim: Another view says God asked both what the object was and what Moses held in his right hand, with the staff’s uses answering the latter.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p321/r8.anchor: وقيل: سأله تعالى عن شيئين عن العصا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p321/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p321/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p321/r9.claim: He rejects that analysis: بيمينك is not a question, and Moses first mentions his own benefit, then the benefit to his flock.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p321/r9.anchor: وفي التحقيق ليس قوله بيمينك بسؤال

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p321/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p321/r10.speaker: النخعي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p321/r10.claim: The majority read وأهش with ḍamma on hāʾ and shīn; al-Nakhaʿī reads it with kasra, with the same sense and an omitted object, leaves.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p321/r10.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور وأهش بضم الهاء والشين المعجمة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p321/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p321/r11.speaker: أبو الفضل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p321/r11.claim: Abū al-Faḍl allows a root meaning to bend foliage or grass toward the flock while tending it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p321/r11.anchor: ويحتمل ذلك أن يكون من هش يهش هشاشة إذا مال

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p321/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p321/r12.speaker: الحسن وعكرمة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p321/r12.claim: Al-Ḥasan and ʿIkrima read وأهس with unpointed sīn, meaning to drive the flock.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p321/r12.anchor: وقرأ الحسن وعكرمة: وأهس بضم الهاء والسين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p321/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p321/r13.speaker: ابن خالويه
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p321/r13.claim: Ibn Khālawayh attributes to al-Nakhaʿī a quadriliteral reading وأهس with a hamza bearing ḍamma.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p321/r13.anchor: ونقل ابن خالويه عن النخعي أنه قرأ وأهس بضم الهمزة من أهس رباعيا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p321/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p321/r14.speaker: صاحب اللوامح
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p321/r14.claim: The author of al-Lawāmiʿ reports from ʿIkrima and Mujāhid a softened-shīn reading, apparently avoiding doubled shīn because its frication is heavy.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p321/r14.anchor: وذكر صاحب اللوامح عن عكرمة ومجاهد وأهش بضم الهاء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p321/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p321/r15.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p321/r15.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī reports al-Nakhaʿī’s quadriliteral form with ḍamma on hamza and shīn; both roots evoke brittle bread crumbling.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p321/r15.anchor: وذكر الزمخشري عن النخعي أنه قرأ وأهش بضم الهمزة والشين المعجمة من أهش رباعيا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p321/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p321/r16.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p321/r16.claim: Moses lists ordinary benefits because he senses an extraordinary event is coming; the miracle will eclipse every use he has just named. The stick was called nabʿa.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p321/r16.anchor: ذكر على التفصيل والإجمال المنافع المتعلقة بالعصا كأنه أحس بما يعقب هذا السؤال من أمر عظيم يحدثه الله تعالى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p322/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p322/r1.speaker: فرقة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p322/r1.claim: One group reads غنمي with a quiescent nūn; another vocalizes the construction so the verb acts directly on the flock.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p322/r1.anchor: وقرأت فرقة غنمي بسكون النون وفرقة على غنمي بإيقاع الفعل على الغنم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p322/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p322/r2.speaker: المفسرون
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p322/r2.claim: Commentators list practical uses: the forked stick and hook bend or break branches, carry gear, provide shade, extend a short rope, and protect the flock from predators.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p322/r2.anchor: والمآرب ذكر المفسرون أنها كانت ذات شعبتين ومحجن فإذا طال الغصن حناه بالمحجن

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p322/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p322/r3.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p322/r3.claim: One account attributes further miracles to the staff: drawing water, changing its forks to a bucket or lights, fighting enemies, bearing fruit, following Moses with provisions, producing springs, guarding against vermin, and gathering distant sheep.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p322/r3.anchor: وقيل: كان فيها من المعجزات أنه كان يستقي بها فتطول

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p322/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p322/r4.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p322/r4.claim: The staff was said to come from the prophetic staffs kept with Shuʿayb, brought from Paradise by Adam, and to measure ten cubits; another report gives twelve cubits by Moses’ measure.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p322/r4.anchor: وهذه العصا أخذها من بيت عصي الأنبياء التي كانت عند شعيب حين اتفقا على الرعية هبط بها آدم من الجنة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p322/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p322/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p322/r5.claim: Although مآرب is plural, أخرى is feminine singular as if the plural were one feminine noun; this is allowed generally and better suits the verse endings.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p322/r5.anchor: وعامل المآرب وإن كان جمعا معاملة الواحدة المؤنثة فأتبعها صفتها في قوله أخرى ولم يقل آخر رعيا للفواصل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p322/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p322/r6.speaker: الزهري وشيبة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p322/r6.claim: Al-Zuhrī and Shayba are reported to read مارب without a fully articulated hamza, apparently easing it between vowel qualities.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p322/r6.anchor: وقرأ الزهري وشيبة: مارب بغير همز

AKHFASH:v2p443/r4.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v2p443/r4.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v2p443/r4.claim: The singular of مآرب is مأربة.

SAMIN-DURR:20:18/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:18/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:18/r1.claim: هي refers back to the thing Moses was asked about.

SAMIN-DURR:20:18/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:18/r2.speaker: الجحدري، ابن أبي إسحاق
SAMIN-DURR:20:18/r2.claim: The common reading has open yāʾ in عصاي; al-Jahdari and Ibn Abi Ishaq read عصي with metathesis and assimilation, referring to an earlier discussion of the dialect.
SAMIN-DURR:20:18/r2.anchor: الجحدري وابن أبي إسحاق " عصي " بالقلب والإدغام

SAMIN-DURR:20:18/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:18/r3.speaker: أبو عمرو، ابن أبي إسحاق
SAMIN-DURR:20:18/r3.claim: Abu Amr and Ibn Abi Ishaq are also reported with a quiescent yāʾ in وصل; Nafiʿ similarly joins two quiescent letters in محياي.
SAMIN-DURR:20:18/r3.anchor: وروي عن أبي عمرو وابن أبي إسحاق أيضا " عصاي " بسكونها وصلا

SAMIN-DURR:20:18/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:18/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:18/r4.claim: أتوكأ may be a second predicate of هي, a circumstantial clause from عصاي or the yāʾ (the latter is remote), or a new independent sentence.
SAMIN-DURR:20:18/r4.anchor: يجوز أن يكون خبرا ثانيا ل " هي " ، ويجوز أن يكون حالا: إما من " عصاي "

SAMIN-DURR:20:18/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:18/r5.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:20:18/r5.claim: Abu al-Baqa reports a parse with عصاي as the object of an omitted verb and أتوكأ as predicate; the author says not to adopt it.
SAMIN-DURR:20:18/r5.anchor: وجوز أبو البقاء نقلا عن غيره أن تكون " عصاي " منصوبة بفعل مقدر، و " أتوكأ " هو الخبر، ولا ينبغي أن يقال ذلك

SAMIN-DURR:20:18/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:18/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:18/r6.claim: التوكؤ means leaning one's weight on something, synonymous with الاتكاء; the words share a root but differ in pattern.
SAMIN-DURR:20:18/r6.anchor: والتوكؤ: التحامل على الشيء، وهو بمعنى الاتكاء. وقد تقدم تفسيره في يوسف فهما من مادة واحدة

SAMIN-DURR:20:18/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:18/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:18/r7.claim: With dotted shīn, الهش means beating or shaking foliage down; the object “leaves/trees” is omitted in the readings.
SAMIN-DURR:20:18/r7.anchor: والهش بالمعجمة الخبط. يقال: هششت الورق أهشه أي: خبطته ليسقط

SAMIN-DURR:20:18/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:18/r8.speaker: النخعي
SAMIN-DURR:20:18/r8.claim: The kasra form هش يهش means friendliness; al-Nakhai reads it, explained either like the common form or as bending from هشاشة.
SAMIN-DURR:20:18/r8.anchor: وأما هش يهش بكسر العين في المضارع فبمعنى البشاشة، وقد قرأ النخعي بذلك

SAMIN-DURR:20:18/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:18/r9.speaker: الحسن، عكرمة
SAMIN-DURR:20:18/r9.claim: Al-Hasan and Ikrima read وأهس with unpointed sīn, meaning drive or herd; it takes على here by inclusion of a verb that governs that preposition.
SAMIN-DURR:20:18/r9.anchor: وقرأ الحسن وعكرمة " وأهس " بضم الهاء والسين المهملة وهو السوق

SAMIN-DURR:20:18/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:18/r10.speaker: النخعي
SAMIN-DURR:20:18/r10.claim: Ibn Khalawayh transmits a form-IV Nakhai reading with unpointed sīn; al-Zamakhshari's dotted-shīn transmission may represent another reading.

SAMIN-DURR:20:18/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:18/r11.speaker: مجاهد، عكرمة
SAMIN-DURR:20:18/r11.claim: Al-Lawāmiḥ reports Mujahid and Ikrima with light shīn; the author says it may be a reduction of the doubled consonant, with the common reading's sense.
SAMIN-DURR:20:18/r11.anchor: ونقل صاحب " اللوامح " عن مجاهد وعكرمة

SAMIN-DURR:20:18#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:18#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:18#2/r1.claim: Some read غنمي with a quiescent nūn, a form the author says is not productive by analogy.
SAMIN-DURR:20:18#2/r1.anchor: وقرأ بعضهم " غنمي " بسكون النون ولا ينقاس

SAMIN-DURR:20:18#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:18#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:18#2/r2.claim: مآرب is the plural of مأربة, “need”; إربة also means need, and the rāʾ of مأربة occurs with all three vowelings.
SAMIN-DURR:20:18#2/r2.anchor: والمآرب: جمع مأربة وهي الحاجة وكذلك الإربة أيضا. وفي راء " المأربة " الحركات الثلاث

SAMIN-DURR:20:18#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:18#2/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:18#2/r3.claim: The feminine singular أخرى agrees with the non-rational plural مآرب, as in الأسماء الحسنى at 17:110.

SAMIN-DURR:20:18#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:18#2/r4.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:20:18#2/r4.claim: Abu al-Baqa says أخر would instead agree with the surface plural form.
SAMIN-DURR:20:18#2/r4.anchor: قال أبو البقاء: " ولو قيل " أخر " لكان على اللفظ

SAMIN-DURR:20:18#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:18#2/r5.speaker: شيبة، الزهري
SAMIN-DURR:20:18#2/r5.claim: Shayba and al-Zuhri are reported with مارب without a fully articulated hamza; the author takes this as hamza between full articulation and deletion.
SAMIN-DURR:20:18#2/r5.anchor: ونقل الأهوازي عن شيبة والزهري " مارب " قال " بغير همز " كذا أطلق

ZAJJAJ:v3p353#2/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p353#2/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p353#2/r3.claim: عصى without alif is also read and is a Hudhayl dialect, but Zajjaj considers عصاي the better form.
ZAJJAJ:v3p353#2/r3.anchor: وقرئ هي عصى بغير ألف، وأجودهما عصاي. وعصى لغة هذيل.

ZAJJAJ:v3p353#2/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p353#2/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p353#2/r4.claim: Possessive yāʾ normally puts kasra before it; after an alif, dual alif, or an existing yāʾ preceded by kasra, no further change is possible or needed.
ZAJJAJ:v3p353#2/r4.anchor: والأصل في يا الإضافة أن يكسر ما قبلها، تقول هذا حجري فتكسر الراء

ZAJJAJ:v3p353#2/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p353#2/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p353#2/r5.claim: Hudhayl substitutes yāʾ for the unchangeable alif instead of adding a kasra; grammarians attest this dialect, and Abu Dhuʾayb's هوي is cited as poetic evidence.
ZAJJAJ:v3p353#2/r5.anchor: فجعلت هذيل بدلا من كسرة الألف تغييرها إلى الياء، وليس أحد من النحويين إلا وقد حكى هذه اللغة.

ZAJJAJ:v3p353#2/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p353#2/r6.speaker: أبو ذؤيب
ZAJJAJ:v3p353#2/r6.claim: Abu Dhuʾayb's line, including سبقوا هوي, is cited as evidence for the Hudhayl possessive-yāʾ usage.
ZAJJAJ:v3p353#2/r6.anchor: قال أبو ذؤيب. سبقوا هوي وأعنقوا لهواهم. . . فتخرموا ولكل جنب مصرع

ZAJJAJ:v3p354/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p354/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p354/r1.claim: Exegetes explain أهش بها as beating foliage from trees with the staff; its derivation is making something soft and accessible.
ZAJJAJ:v3p354/r1.anchor: جاء في التفسير أخبط بها الشجر، واشتقاقه من أني أحيل الشيء إلى الهشاشة

ZAJJAJ:v3p354/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p354/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p354/r2.claim: مآرب means needs, as in the language; its singular forms are مأربة and مآربة.
ZAJJAJ:v3p354/r2.anchor: جاء في التفسير حاجات أخر، وكذلك هو في اللغة، وواحد المآرب مأربة وماربة.

ZAJJAJ:v3p354/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p354/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p354/r3.claim: أخرى is singular feminine because مآرب denotes a collective of needs; the plural أخر would also be correct.
ZAJJAJ:v3p354/r3.anchor: على لفظ صفة الواحدة، لأن مآرب في معنى جماعة

ASAD-NOTES:20:18/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:20:18/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:20:18/r1.claim: Moses uses his staff to lean on and beat leaves for his sheep, among other purposes.
ASAD-NOTES:20:18/r1.anchor: It is my staff; I lean on it; a nd with it I beat down leaves for my sheep

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1084/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1084/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1084/r3.claim: The question is about the first-person yāʾ, not only forms such as ليَ and لي; its vowel may be open or unvowelled where language and transmitted Qur'anic readings permit.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1084/r3.anchor: هذه مسألة ياء المتكلم فتح ياء المتكلم وعدم فتحها ولا تتعلق فقط بـ (ليَ ولي)

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1084/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1084/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1084/r4.claim: The first-person yāʾ must be opened after a maqṣūr noun, an inflected noun ending in a necessary alif; this explains عصايَ, هدايَ and محيايَ.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1084/r4.anchor: والاسم المقصور هو الإسم المُعرَب الذي آخره ألف لازمة

IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r1.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r1.speaker: نافع
IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r1.claim: Nāfiʿ opens the listed first-person yāʾs except ولي فيها and أخي اشدد, where he uses sukūn.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r1.anchor: ففتحهن نافع إلا اثنتين قوله ﴿ ولي فيها مآرب ﴾ وقوله ﴿ أخي اشدد ﴾ فإنه أسكنهما

IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r2.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r2.speaker: أبو عمرو
IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r2.claim: Abū ʿAmr uses sukūn on ولي فيها and حشرتني أعمى, opening the other listed first-person yāʾs.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r2.anchor: وأسكن أبو عمرو منها اثنتين / ولى فيها مئارب / و ﴿ لم حشرتني أعمى ﴾ وفتح سائرها

IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r3.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r3.speaker: ابن كثير
IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r3.claim: Ibn Kathīr uses sukūn on ولي فيها، ويسر لي أمري، لذكري إن، على عيني إذ, and برأسي إني; he opens the rest.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r3.anchor: وأسكن ابن كثير منها خمسا / ولى فيها مئارب / و ﴿ ويسر لي أمري ﴾ و ﴿ لذكري إن ﴾

IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r4.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r4.speaker: حمزة، الكسائي، ابن عامر، عاصم عن أبي بكر
IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r4.claim: These readers use sukūn on all listed first-person yāʾs.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r4.anchor: وأسكنها كلها حمزة والكسائى وابن عامر وعاصم فى رواية أبى بكر

IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r5.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r5.speaker: حفص عن عاصم
IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r5.claim: Ḥafṣ from ʿĀṣim opens ولي فيها; it is his only opened yāʾ among the listed forms.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r5.anchor: وفتح عاصم فى رواية حفص واحدة قوله تعالى / ولى فيها مئارب /

NASHR:v2p172/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p172/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p172/r1.claim: Al-Azraq from Warsh opens the possessive yāʾ in ولي فيها مآرب; this is among the five listed places where ولي is read with an open yāʾ.
NASHR:v2p172/r1.anchor: وافقه في ولي فيها مآرب في طه الأزرق عن ورش

QIRAAT-ER:20:18:11#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:20:18:11#1/r1.speaker: Y-iḍ
QIRAAT-ER:20:18:11#1/r1.claim: The canonical variant shortens the possessive yāʾ with sukūn rather than fatḥa, described as a pausal versus connected form.
QIRAAT-ER:20:18:11#1/r1.anchor: Y-iḍ, mutawatir: Canonical variant: shortened form without final fatḥa — yāʾ al-iḍāfa read with sukūn instead of fatḥa

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p16#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p16#2/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p16#2/r1.claim: Qatada says Moses shook or beat the tree with his staff to knock down fodder for his sheep.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p16#2/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ وأهش بها على غنمي ﴾ قال أخبط بها الشجر

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p16#2/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p16#2/r2.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p16#2/r2.claim: Qatada glosses the other uses of the staff as other needs and benefits.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p16#2/r2.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ مآرب أخرى ﴾ قال حاجات أخرى منافع أخرى

ALUSI-FULL:v16p174#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p174#3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p174#3/r1.claim: Moses calls the staff his to explain why it is in his right hand and to prepare for the actions he will describe; naming it also prolongs the pleasure of intimate conversation.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p174#3/r1.anchor: نسبها عليه السلام إلى نفسه تحقيقا لوجه كونها بيمينه وتمهيدا لما يعقبه من الأفاعيل المنسوبة اليه

ALUSI-FULL:v16p174#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p174#3/r2.speaker: مقاتل
ALUSI-FULL:v16p174#3/r2.claim: The source says Muqatil reports that the staff's name was Nabʿa.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p174#3/r2.anchor: واسمها على ما روى عن مقاتل نبعة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p174#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p174#3/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p174#3/r3.claim: The staff was taken from the house of the prophets' staffs kept with Shu'ayb when Moses was hired to shepherd; Adam had brought it down from the Garden.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p174#3/r3.anchor: وكان عليه السلام قد اخذها من بيت عصى الأنبياء عليهم السلام التي كانت عند شعيب حين أستاجره للرعى هبط بها آدم عليه السلام من الجنة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p174#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p174#3/r4.speaker: وهب
ALUSI-FULL:v16p174#3/r4.claim: Wahb says the staff was made from a thorn tree and was ten cubits long, equal to Moses' height; another account gives twelve cubits measured by Moses' cubit.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p174#3/r4.anchor: وقال وهب : كانت من العوسج وطولها عشرة اذرع على مقدار قامته عليه السلام

ALUSI-FULL:v16p174#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p174#3/r5.speaker: ابن أبي إسحاق والجحدري
ALUSI-FULL:v16p174#3/r5.claim: Ibn Abi Ishaq and al-Jahdari read ʿaṣī, changing the alif before the first-person suffix to ya and assimilating it, as in Hudhayl's dialect.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p174#3/r5.anchor: وقرأ ابن أبى إسحق والجحدرى ( عصى ) بقلب الالف ياء

ALUSI-FULL:v16p174#3/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p174#3/r6.speaker: شاعرهم
ALUSI-FULL:v16p174#3/r6.claim: The cited Hudhayli line, including the form huwa, is evidence for the dialect's sound change before the first-person suffix.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p174#3/r6.anchor: قال شاعرهم : سبقوا هوى واعنقوا لهواهم فتخرموا ولكل جنب مصرع

ALUSI-FULL:v16p174#3/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p174#3/r7.speaker: الحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v16p174#3/r7.claim: Al-Hasan reads ʿaṣāya with kasra on the ya to resolve the meeting of two quiescent letters; the reading is also transmitted from Abu Ishaq and Abu Amr.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p174#3/r7.anchor: وقرأ الحسن ( عصاى ) بكسر الياء وهي مروية عن أبى ابن إسحاق أيضا وابى عمرو

ALUSI-FULL:v16p174#3/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p174#3/r8.speaker: ابن أبي إسحاق
ALUSI-FULL:v16p174#3/r8.claim: Another reading from Ibn Abi Ishaq leaves the ya quiescent, apparently treating it as paused and tolerating the two quiescent letters.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p174#3/r8.anchor: وعن ابن أبى إسحاق ( عصاى ) بسكون الياء كأنه اعتبر الوقف ولم يبال بالتقاء الساكنين

ALUSI-FULL:v16p174#3/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p174#3/r9.speaker: الفراء
ALUSI-FULL:v16p174#3/r9.claim: The noun ʿaṣā is grammatically feminine without a feminine ending; al-Farra calls this the first solecism heard in Iraq: hādhihi ʿaṣātī.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p174#3/r9.anchor: وأول لحن سمع بالعراق كما قال الفراء : هذه عصاتى

ALUSI-FULL:v16p174#3/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p174#3/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p174#3/r10.claim: The plural forms of ʿaṣā include ʿiṣī with kasra or damma initially, aʿṣ, and aʿṣāʾ.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p174#3/r10.anchor: وتجمع على عصى بكسر أوله وضمه وأعص وأعصاء

ALUSI-FULL:v16p174#3/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p174#3/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p174#3/r11.claim: Atawakkaʾu means that Moses leans on the staff while walking or standing by the flock.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p174#3/r11.anchor: اى أتحامل عليها في المشى والوقوف على رأس القطيع

ALUSI-FULL:v16p174#3/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p174#3/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p174#3/r12.claim: Ahushshu means to strike tree branches with the staff so leaves fall for the sheep to eat; the object is omitted.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p174#3/r12.anchor: اخبط بها ورق الشجر واضربه ليسقط

ALUSI-FULL:v16p174#3/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p174#3/r13.speaker: النخعي
ALUSI-FULL:v16p174#3/r13.claim: Al-Nakha'i reads ahishshu with kasra on the ha, retaining the same sense and an omitted object.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p174#3/r13.anchor: وقرأ النخعى كما ذكر أبو فضل الرازي وابن عطية ( أهش ) بكسر الهاء

ALUSI-FULL:v16p174#3/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p174#3/r14.speaker: أبو الفضل
ALUSI-FULL:v16p174#3/r14.claim: Abu al-Fadl offers a different intransitive sense: the word can mean lean toward the flock with the staff, dropping leaves or otherwise helping them.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p174#3/r14.anchor: وقال أبو الفضل : يحتمل أن يكون ذلك من هش يهش هشاشه إذا مال

ALUSI-FULL:v16p174#3/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p174#3/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p174#3/r15.claim: Another lexical explanation says leaves, grass, or plants are described as hashsha when they dry, soften, and become tender; on this reading no object is omitted.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p174#3/r15.anchor: ويقال : هش الورق والكلأ والنبات إذا جف ولان

ALUSI-FULL:v16p175/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p175/r1.speaker: الحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v16p175/r1.claim: Al-Hasan reads ahussu with damma on the ha and an ungeminated s; hass means to drive sheep, with ʿala conveying bending over them as if to strike.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p175/r1.anchor: وقرأ الحسن ( اهس ) بضم الهاء والسين المهملة من الهس

ALUSI-FULL:v16p175/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p175/r2.speaker: القاموس
ALUSI-FULL:v16p175/r2.claim: The Qamus says hass and hashsh can both mean breaking or crushing something.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p175/r2.anchor: وفي كتاب السين والشين لصاحب القاموس يقال هس الشئ وهشه إذا فته وكسره فهما بمعنى

ALUSI-FULL:v16p175/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p175/r3.speaker: النخعي
ALUSI-FULL:v16p175/r3.claim: Ibn Khalawayh transmits an al-Nakha'i reading from the quadriliteral form ahashsha.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p175/r3.anchor: ونقل ابن خالويه عن النخعى أنه قرأ ( أهش ) من أهش رباعيا

ALUSI-FULL:v16p175/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p175/r4.speaker: عكرمة ومجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v16p175/r4.claim: Al-Lawamiʿ reports Ikrimah and Mujahid reading ahushshu with a light sh; its explanation as the doubled form is possible, but Alusi calls that account very far-fetched.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p175/r4.anchor: وذكر صاحب اللوامح عن عكرمة ومجاهد أهش بضم الهاء وتخفيف الشين المعجمه ثم قال : لا اعرف وجهه

ALUSI-FULL:v16p175/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p175/r5.speaker: جماعة
ALUSI-FULL:v16p175/r5.claim: Some read ghanami with a still nun, while another group reads the form analyzed with ʿala as a preposition and ghanami as the direct object; Alusi cannot identify that group's verb reading.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p175/r5.anchor: وقرأت جماعة غنمي بسكون النون واخرى على غنمى على أن على جار ومجرور غنمى مفعول صريح للفعل السابق

ALUSI-FULL:v16p175/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p175/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p175/r6.claim: Ghanam is a feminine collective noun for sheep of either sex, with no singular from the same form; its singular is shāh, diminutive ghanīmah, and it has several plurals and a dual for two flocks.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p175/r6.anchor: والغنم الشاة وهو اسم مؤنث موضوع للجنس يقع على الذكر والاناث وعليهم جميعا ولا واحد له من لفظه وإنما واحدة شاه

ALUSI-FULL:v16p175/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p175/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p175/r7.claim: Moses first mentions the staff's benefit to himself, then its benefit to his flock, perhaps because he had just leaned on it and that came to mind first.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p175/r7.anchor: وقدم عليه السلام بيان مصلحة نفسه في قوله اتوكأ عليها وثنى بمصلحة رعيته

ALUSI-FULL:v16p175/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p175/r8.speaker: أحمد
ALUSI-FULL:v16p175/r8.claim: Ahmad transmits that after God called Moses near, he clutched the staff and struggled upright while trembling, speechless and terrified, then crept to the tree before God asked what he held.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p175/r8.anchor: وقد روى الامام أحمد أنه عليه السلام بعد أن ناده ربه سبحانه وتحقق أنه جل وعلا هو المنادى

ALUSI-FULL:v16p175/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p175/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p175/r9.claim: Alusi suggests Moses may have mentioned leaning first because it best fit God's question about what was in his right hand.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p175/r9.anchor: وقيل : لعل تقديم التوكؤ عليها لأنه الاوفق للسؤال بما تلك بيمينك

ALUSI-FULL:v16p175/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p175/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p175/r10.claim: Moses then summarizes the staff's remaining uses with the phrase that he has other needs for it.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p175/r10.anchor: اجمل اوصافها في قوله ( ولى فيها مارب اخرى

ALUSI-FULL:v16p175#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p175#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p175#2/r1.claim: مأرب is a singular form with three possible vowels on its rāʾ; it is treated as singular in the adjective, a permissible and especially apt agreement at a verse ending.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p175#2/r1.anchor: ومفردة مأربه مثلثة الراء وعومل في الوصف معاملة مفرده فلم يقل أخر

ALUSI-FULL:v16p175#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p175#2/r2.speaker: الزهر وشيبه
ALUSI-FULL:v16p175#2/r2.claim: Al-Ahwāzī reports that al-Zuhrī and Shayba read مآرب without a fully articulated hamza, apparently softening it between hamza and vowel.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p175#2/r2.anchor: عن الزهر وشيبه أنهما قرأ ( مارب ) بغير همز

ALUSI-FULL:v16p175#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p175#2/r3.speaker: وهب
ALUSI-FULL:v16p175#2/r3.claim: A report transmitted by Aḥmad and others from Wahb describes a forked staff with a hook used to bend or break branches, carry gear, make shade, reach water, and defend the flock.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p175#2/r3.anchor: روى الامام أحمد وغيره عن وهب في تعين هذه المآرب أنه كان لها شعبتان ومحجم تحتهما

ALUSI-FULL:v16p175#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p175#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v16p175#2/r4.claim: Al-Ṭabrisī attributes many of the further marvels recounted about the staff to Ibn ʿAbbās; another unnamed account says it could draw water, bear fruit, produce springs, speak, and ward off pests.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p175#2/r4.anchor: ونقل الطبرسى كثيرا مما ذكر عن ابن عباس رضى الله تعالى عنهما

ALUSI-FULL:v16p175#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p175#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p175#2/r5.claim: One explanation is that God prompts Moses to enumerate the staff’s many ordinary benefits before displaying a far greater benefit; the distant demonstrative and vocative signal its importance, while the list and “other uses” magnify its many functions. Naming the staff lets Moses attach these predicates and avoids redundancy.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p175#2/r5.anchor: أن يعدد المرافق الكثيرة التي علقها بالعصا ويستكثرها ويستعظمها ثم يريه تعالى عقب ذلك الآية العظيمة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p175#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p175#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p175#2/r6.claim: An alternative reads the exchange as Moses presenting the seemingly insignificant dry stick so God can reveal the great power by which He transforms a humble thing; on this reading ما asks for its description or its kind, and تلك belittles it.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p175#2/r6.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون المراد اظهاره عليه السلام حقارتها ليريه عز وجل عظيم ما يخترعه في الخشبة اليابسة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p175#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p175#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p175#2/r7.claim: Another proposal is that Moses was awed by the signs and the question eased his fear; the repeated address consoles him, and his vague mention of other uses may invite another question and prolong the beloved conversation.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p175#2/r7.anchor: غلبت عليه الدهشة والهيبة فسأله سبحانه وتكلم معه ازالة لتلك الهيبة والدهشة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p175#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p175#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p175#2/r8.claim: Within the awe explanation, the distal demonstrative can portray the staff as far away because Moses is distracted by awe; the unstated further uses might be a bid to hear God speak longer.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p175#2/r8.anchor: لتنزيل العصا منزلة البعيد لغفلته عليه السلام عنها بما غلب عليه من ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v16p175#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p175#2/r9.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v16p175#2/r9.claim: Some say God establishes that it is a stick so Moses will not fear when it becomes a snake; al-Ālūsī rejects this proposal, and likewise rejects splitting the exchange into two questions and two answers.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p175#2/r9.anchor: وزعم بعضهم أنه تعالى سأله عليه السلام ليقرره على أنها خشبة حتى إذا قلبها حية لا يخافها وليس بشئ

ALUSI-FULL:v16p175#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p175#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p175#2/r10.claim: The proposals that God first asked what the object was and then what Moses did with it, or separately asked what it was and what he held in his right hand, are weak; the question and answer are each single, as the apparent sense indicates.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p175#2/r10.anchor: وعلى جميع هذه الأقوال السؤال واحد والجواب واحد كما هو الظاهر وقيل

ALUSI-FULL:v16p177/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p177/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p177/r1.claim: The verse supports the recommendation of leaning on a staff even for someone who does not need it as a bowstring support.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p177/r1.anchor: استدل بالاية على استحباب التوكؤ على العصا وان لم يكن الشخص بحيث تكون وترا لقوسه

ALUSI-FULL:v16p177/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p177/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p177/r2.claim: The verse supports economy in grazing: tap branches so leaves fall without stripping them, allowing regrowth for others to use.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p177/r2.anchor: وعلى استحباب الاقتصاد في المرعى بالهش وهو ضرب الشجر ليسقط الورق دون الاستئصال ليخلف

ALUSI-FULL:v16p210/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p210/r3.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v16p210/r3.claim: Another explanation says God first showed Moses perfect divinity, then human limitation: asking about the staff's uses showed how even a present object exceeds what reason can know without divine guidance.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p210/r3.anchor: لما عرفه كمال الالوهية اراد أن يعرفه نقصان البشرية فسأله عن منافع العصا

ALUSI-FULL:v16p211/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p211/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p211/r11.claim: Al-Alūsī contrasts Muhammad's report that his sight neither swerved nor transgressed with Moses' simple answer about his staff, seeing a clear difference in their ranks.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p211/r11.anchor: وانظر إلى الفرق بين قوله تعالى عن نبينا

ALUSI-FULL:v16p211/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p211/r12.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v16p211/r12.claim: Some add that Moses leaned on his staff while Muhammad relied on God's grace, citing Muhammad's assurance that God suffices him and his believing followers.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p211/r12.anchor: وذكر بعضهم أن في الآيات ما يشعر بالفرق بينهما أيضا عليهما الصلاة والسلام من وجه أخر

ALUSI-FULL:v16p211/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p211/r13.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v16p211/r13.claim: Some say Moses first named his own needs and then his flock, whereas Muhammad cared only for his community, praying for their guidance; at judgment Moses says 'myself' and Muhammad 'my community.'
ALUSI-FULL:v16p211/r13.anchor: بدأ بمصالح نفسه فى قوله : ( أتوكأ عليها ) ثم مصالح رعيته

ALUSI-FULL:v16p211/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p211/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p211/r14.claim: Al-Alūsī warns readers not to emulate these comparisons, which he says have only a very slight basis; he quoted them to prevent being impressed by them.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p211/r14.anchor: ولعمرى أنه لاينبغى أن يقتدى به فى مثل هذا الكلام كما لايخفى على ذوى الافهام

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p268#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p268#2/r4.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p268#2/r4.claim: One report describes the staff as having two branches, two prongs at its base, and a hook.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p268#2/r4.anchor: قيل: وكانت لها شعبتان، وفي أسفلها سنان، ولها محجن

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p268#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p268#2/r5.speaker: مقاتل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p268#2/r5.claim: Muqātil gives the staff's name as Nabʿa.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p268#3/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p268#3/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p268#3/r1.claim: Moses leans on it while walking, tired, and jumping.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p268#3/r1.anchor: {أتوكأ عليها} أعتمد عليها إذا مشيت وإذا أعييت وعند الوثبة،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p268#3/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p268#3/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p268#3/r2.claim: He strikes dry trees so leaves fall for his sheep to eat.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p268#3/r2.anchor: {وأهش بها على غنمي} أضرب بها الشجرة اليابسة ليسقط ورقها فترعاه الغنم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p268#3/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p268#3/r3.speaker: عكرمة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p268#3/r3.claim: ʿIkrima reads ahus with unpointed sīn, meaning to drive sheep; hass means driving sheep.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p268#3/r3.anchor: وقرأ عكرمة " وأهس " بالسين غير المعجمة، أي: أزجر بها الغنم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p268#3/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p268#3/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p268#3/r4.claim: Maʾārib means needs or benefits; it is the plural of maʾraba with fatḥa or ḍamma on rāʾ.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p268#3/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p268#3/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p268#3/r5.claim: The feminine plural ukhar is omitted because the verse ending calls for this wording.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p268#3/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p268#3/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p268#3/r6.claim: Travel uses included carrying provisions, drawing water, killing snakes, fighting predators, and providing shade.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p268#3/r6.anchor: وكان يحمل بها الزاد ويشد بها الحبل

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p268#3/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p268#3/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p268#3/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports the staff moved and spoke, produced food and water, bore fruit, lengthened into a bucket, lit the night, and fought enemies.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p268#3/r7.anchor: وروي عن ابن عباس: أن موسى كان يحمل عليها زاده وسقاءه، فجعلت متماشيه وتحدثه

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:17-19/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:17-19/r4.speaker: قُرئ
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:17-19/r4.claim: Aṣī is a dialectal reading of the Hudhayl tribe.

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:17-19/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:17-19/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:17-19/r5.claim: Moses leans on the staff when tired or when standing at the head of the flock.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:17-19/r5.anchor: { أتوكؤا عليها } أعتمد عليها إذا أعييت أو وقفت على رأس القطيع.

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:17-19/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:17-19/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:17-19/r6.claim: He shakes leaves from branches over his sheep; the reading is related to brittle bread breaking apart.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:17-19/r6.anchor: { وأهش بها على غنمى } وأخبط الورق بها على رؤوس غنمي، وقرىء { أهش } وكلاهما من هش الخبز يهش إذا انكسر لهشاشته

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:17-19/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:17-19/r7.speaker: قُرئ
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:17-19/r7.claim: A reading with sīn derives from driving sheep and means directing them with the staff.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:17-19/r7.anchor: وقرىء بالسين من الهس وهو زجر الغنم أي أنحى عليها زاجرا لها.

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:17-19/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:17-19/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:17-19/r8.claim: Other uses include carrying tools, hanging a garment for shade, extending a short rope, and fighting predators threatening the sheep.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:17-19/r8.anchor: إذا سار ألقاها على عاتقه فعلق بها أدواته

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:17-19/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:17-19/r10.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:17-19/r10.claim: Its later feats, including light, a bucket, lengthening, defense, water, leaves, and fruit, are signs created by God, not inherent properties.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:17-19/r10.anchor: على أن ذلك آيات باهرة ومعجزات قاهرة أحدثها الله فيها لأجله وليست من خواصها

DURR-FULL:v5p564/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p564/r1.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v5p564/r1.claim: Qatada explains that Moses beat foliage from trees with the staff to feed his sheep.
DURR-FULL:v5p564/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله: {وأهش بها على غنمي} قال: أخبط بها الشجر

DURR-FULL:v5p564/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p564/r2.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v5p564/r2.claim: Qatada glosses the staff's other uses as other needs.
DURR-FULL:v5p564/r2.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله: {وأهش بها على غنمي}

DURR-FULL:v5p564/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p564/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p564/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas likewise says the staff served other needs.
DURR-FULL:v5p564/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله: {ولي فيها مآرب أخرى} قال: حوائج

DURR-FULL:v5p564/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p564/r4.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v5p564/r4.claim: Mujahid interprets the other uses as needs and benefits.
DURR-FULL:v5p564/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد رضي الله عنه في قوله: {مآرب أخرى} قال: حاجات ومنافع

DURR-FULL:v5p564/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p564/r5.speaker: السدي
DURR-FULL:v5p564/r5.claim: Al-Suddi says Moses carried his provisions bag and waterskin on the staff.

DURR-FULL:v5p564/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p564/r6.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v5p564/r6.claim: Qatada says the staff illuminated Moses at night and had belonged to Adam.
DURR-FULL:v5p564/r6.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله: {ولي فيها مآرب أخرى} قال: كانت تضيء له بالليل وكانت عصا آدم

BURSEVI:v5p286#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p286#3/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p286#3/r5.claim: Moses calls it my staff to establish that it is in his right hand and prepare for the later actions attributed to him.
BURSEVI:v5p286#3/r5.anchor: نسبها إلى نفسه تحقيقا لوجه كونها بيمينه وتمهيدا لما يعقبه من الأفاعيل المنسوبة إليه عليه السلام

BURSEVI:v5p286#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p286#3/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p286#3/r6.claim: He leans on the staff when weary during travel, while walking, and while standing near the flock at pasture.
BURSEVI:v5p286#3/r6.anchor: اعتمد عليها عند الإعياء في الطريق وحال المشي وحين الوقوف على رأس القطيع في المرعى

BURSEVI:v5p286#3/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p286#3/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p286#3/r7.claim: Hashsh means striking foliage with a staff so it falls; Moses knocks leaves from trees onto the sheep’s heads for them to eat.
BURSEVI:v5p286#3/r7.anchor: يقال هش الورق يهشه ويهشه خبطه بعصا

BURSEVI:v5p286#3/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p286#3/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p286#3/r8.claim: Maʾārib is plural of maʾriba, with rāʾ read with fatḥa or ḍamma; ukhrā is feminine to match the pause-ending cadence.
BURSEVI:v5p286#3/r8.anchor: جمع مأربة بفتح الراء وضمها وهي الحاجة

BURSEVI:v5p286#3/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p286#3/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p286#3/r9.claim: Beyond leaning and shaking down leaves, the staff serves as a shoulder pole for a bow, quiver, milk pail, and water flask, carries provisions, and provides company on the road.
BURSEVI:v5p286#3/r9.anchor: إذا سار ألقاها على عاتقه وعلق بها قوسه وكنانته وحلابه ومطهرته وحمل عليها زاده وتحدثه

BURSEVI:v5p286#3/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p286#3/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p286#3/r10.claim: Its forked end and hook could bend or twist branches to break them; a point at the bottom could be planted to draw water, and its forks could act as a bucket in a well, with the staff extending a short rope.
BURSEVI:v5p286#3/r10.anchor: وكان لها شعبتان ومحجن فإذا طال الغصن حناه بالمحجن وإذا حاول كسره لواه بالشعبتين

BURSEVI:v5p286#3/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p286#3/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p286#3/r11.claim: The staff could light the night like a candle, defend Moses against enemies and predators, drive away vermin, and support a cloak as a shade in the wilderness.
BURSEVI:v5p286#3/r11.anchor: وإذا تعرضت لغنمه السباع قاتل بها وتطرد الهوام

BURSEVI:v5p286#3/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p286#3/r12.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p286#3/r12.claim: The staff was twelve cubits by Moses’ measure, made from a myrtle tree in the Garden, and entrusted to Shuʿayb by an angel in human form.
BURSEVI:v5p286#3/r12.anchor: وكانت اثني عشر ذراعا بذراعه عليه السلام من عود آس من شجر الجنة استودعها عند شعيب ملك من الملائكة في صورة إنسان

BURSEVI:v5p287/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p287/r1.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v5p287/r1.claim: Kāshifī says the staff came from the Garden, had two forks, a hook and a lower point, was named ʿAlīq, and passed from Adam to Shuʿayb and then Moses.
BURSEVI:v5p287/r1.anchor: وقال الكاشفي : (آن عصا ازوب مرد بهشت بود طول اوده

BURSEVI:v5p287/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p287/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p287/r2.claim: The staff symbolizes prophets as shepherds of people, who resemble livestock needing guidance and protection from Satan’s wolves and the ego’s lion; people must follow their direction and serve them.
BURSEVI:v5p287/r2.anchor: وفي العصا إشارة إلى أن الأنبياء عليهم السلام رعاة الخلق والخلق مثل البهائم محتاجون إلى الرعي والكلاءة

BURSEVI:v5p287/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p287/r3.speaker: الحافظ
BURSEVI:v5p287/r3.claim: Ḥāfiẓ’s couplet says the shepherd of the valley of Ayman reaches his aim through nine years of devoted service to Shuʿayb.
BURSEVI:v5p287/r3.anchor: شبان وادى ايمن كهى رسد بمراد كه ند سال بجان خدمت شعيب كند

BURSEVI:v5p287/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p287/r4.speaker: بعض أهل المعرفة
BURSEVI:v5p287/r4.claim: Some knowers identify the staff with the tranquil soul, which effaces illusions and imaginings; its serpent form is receptive to faith, as jinn once appeared as snakes in Medina and people were told not to kill them.
BURSEVI:v5p287/r4.anchor: قال بعض أهل المعرفة لما كانت العصا صورة النفس المطمئنة المفنية للموهومات والمتخيلات

BURSEVI:v5p287/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p287/r5.speaker: بعض أهل المعرفة
BURSEVI:v5p287/r5.claim: In this reading, Moses relies on the soul for hidden aims and acquired perfections gained through bodily striving and spiritual discipline; his flock represents his limbs, senses, and natural and bodily powers.
BURSEVI:v5p287/r5.anchor: أي : أستعين بها على مطالبي في السر {وأهش بها على غنمى} أي : على رعايا أعضائي

BURSEVI:v5p287/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p287/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p287/r6.claim: Through struggle and discipline the soul repents, and disobedience turns into obedience, citing God’s promise to replace the repentant’s evil deeds with good deeds.
BURSEVI:v5p287/r6.anchor: فإذا جاهدت وارتاضت وأنابت إلى ربها انقلبت المعصية التي هي السيئة طاعة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p40/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p40/r6.speaker: ابن الجوهري
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p40/r6.claim: A report says God reproached Moses for calling the staff his own, then ordered him to cast it down to show its marvel and that he did not own or control it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p40/r6.anchor: قال ابن الجوهري: وروي في بعض الآثار أن الله تعالى عتب على موسى إضافة العصا إلى نفسه في ذلك الموطن فقيل له ألقها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p40/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p40/r7.speaker: الحسن وأبو عمرو
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p40/r7.claim: Al-Hasan and, according to one transmission, Abu Amr read the final yāʾ with kasra, as in غلامي.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p40/r7.anchor: وقرأ الحسن وأبو عمرو بخلاف عنه «عصاي» بكسر الياء مثل غلامي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p40/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p40/r8.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p40/r8.claim: A group read عصى, identified as Hudhayl dialect; Abu Dhu'ayb's verse is cited as evidence.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p40/r8.anchor: وقرأت فرقة «عصى» وهي لغة هذيل ومنه قول أبي ذؤيب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p40/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p40/r9.speaker: الجمهور
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p40/r9.claim: The majority read the final yāʾ with fatḥa.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p40/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p40/r10.speaker: ابن أبي إسحاق
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p40/r10.claim: Ibn Abi Ishaq read the final yāʾ as quiescent.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p40/r10.anchor: وقرأ ابن أبي إسحاق «عصاي» بياء ساكنة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p40/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p40/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p40/r11.claim: Moses names the staff's principal and greatest uses, then summarizes its other uses.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p40/r11.anchor: ثم ذكر موسى عليه السلام من منافع عصاه عظمها وجمهورها، وأجمل سائر ذلك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p40/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p40/r12.speaker: الجمهور
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p40/r12.claim: The majority read with ḍamma on hāʾ and dotted shīn: beating or shaking trees so leaves fall for the sheep.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p40/r12.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور «وأهش» بضم الهاء والشين المنقوطة ومعناه أخبط بها الشجر حتى ينتثر بها الورق للغنم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p40/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p40/r13.speaker: إبراهيم النخعي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p40/r13.claim: Ibrahim al-Nakha'i reads with kasra on hāʾ, with the same meaning.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p40/r13.anchor: وقرأ إبراهيم النخعي «وأهش» بكسر والمعنى كالذي تقدم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p40/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p40/r14.speaker: عكرمة مولى ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p40/r14.claim: Ikrima reads with undotted sīn; the verb means to drive the sheep away or frighten them.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p40/r14.anchor: وقرأ عكرمة مولى ابن عباس «وأهس» بضم الهاء والسين غير المنقوطة ومعناه أزجر بها وأخوف

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p40/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p40/r15.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p40/r15.claim: One group reads “my sheep” in the genitive.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p40/r16.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p40/r16.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p40/r16.claim: Another reading makes the verb act directly upon “my sheep.”

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p40/r17.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p40/r17.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p40/r17.claim: A group reads the nūn as quiescent; Ibn Atiyya says he knows no justification for this reading.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p40/r17.anchor: وقرأت «غنمي» بسكون النون ولا أعرف لها وجها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p40/r18.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p40/r18.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p40/r18.claim: The feminine singular “other” follows a non-rational plural, which is conventionally treated like a feminine singular; he cites 20:8 and 34:10 as parallels.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p40/r18.anchor: فوحد مع تقدم الجمع وهو المهيع في توابع جمع ما لا يعقل والكناية عنه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p40/r19.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p40/r19.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p40/r19.claim: Moses's staff came from the prophets' staff house kept by Shuayb during their agreement over tending flocks; it had descended from Paradise with Adam and came from the central elongated part of a basil leaf.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p40/r19.anchor: كانت عصا آدم هبط بها من الجنة وكانت من العير الذي في ورق الريحان

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p277#3/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p277#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p277#3/r1.claim: Tawakkūʾ means leaning one's weight on something.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p277#3/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى أتوكأ عليه التوكؤ التحامل على الشيء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p277#3/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p277#3/r2.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p277#3/r2.claim: Al-Farraʾ says ahushshu means striking dry trees so their leaves fall for the sheep to eat.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p277#3/r2.anchor: قال الفراء أضرب بها الشجر اليابس ليسقط ورقه فترعاه غنمي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p277#3/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p277#3/r3.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p277#3/r3.claim: Al-Zajjaj derives ahushshu from turning or moving something toward softness and ease.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p277#3/r3.anchor: قال الزجاج واشتقاقه من أني احيل الشيء إلى الهشاشه والإمكان

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p277#3/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p277#3/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p277#3/r4.claim: Maʾārib means needs or purposes, and its singular is maʾriba or maʾraba.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p277#3/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p277#3/r5.speaker: قتيبة وورش
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p277#3/r5.claim: Qutayba and Warsh incline the hamza in maʾārib.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p277#3/r5.anchor: وروى قتيبة وورش مآرب بامالة الهمزة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p277#3/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p277#3/r8.speaker: ابن عباس ووهب
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p277#3/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas and Wahb say Moses first answered that it was his staff, then supplied its uses in response to a second implicit question.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p277#3/r8.anchor: أحدها أنه أجاب بقوله هي عصاي فقيل له ما تصنع بها فذكر باقي الكلام جوابا عن سؤال ثان قاله ابن عباس ووهب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p277#3/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p277#3/r9.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p277#3/r9.claim: Said ibn Jubayr says Moses explained his need for the staff lest God command him to cast it away, as He had commanded him to remove his sandals.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p277#3/r9.anchor: والثاني أنه انما أظهر فوائدها وبين حاجته اليها خوفا من أن يأمره بالقائها كالنعلين قاله سعيد بن جبير

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p277#3/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p277#3/r10.speaker: الماوردي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p277#3/r10.claim: Al-Mawardi says Moses listed the staff's benefits to show that he was not carrying it idly.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p277#3/r10.anchor: والثالث أنه بين منافعها لئلا يكون عابثا بحملها قاله الماوردي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p277#3/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p277#3/r11.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p277#3/r11.claim: Three explanations are offered for why Moses listed only some benefits: he did not want to be distracted from God's speech, he knew God already knew them, or he chose essential benefits over incidental ones.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p277#3/r11.anchor: فان قيل فلم اقتصر على ذكر بعض منافعها ولم يطل الشرح فعنه ثلاثة أجوبة أحدها أنه كره أن يشتغل عن كلام الله

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p279/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p279/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p279/r1.claim: The remaining explanation for mentioning only some benefits is that Moses named what was essential and left incidental uses aside.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p279/r1.anchor: والثالث أنه اقتصر على اللازم دون العارض

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p279/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p279/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p279/r2.claim: A report says the staff lit the way at night, guarded Moses from vermin, and produced fruit whenever he wanted some.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p279/r2.anchor: وقيل كانت تضيء له بالليل وتدفع عنه الهوام وتثمر له إذا اشتهى الثمار

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p279/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p279/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p279/r3.claim: One view from Ibn Abbas says the staff was made from a myrtle tree of Paradise.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p279/r3.anchor: أحدهما أنها كات من آس الجنة قاله ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p279/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p279/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p279/r4.claim: The other view says the staff was made from buckthorn (ʿawsaj).

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p279/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p279/r5.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p279/r5.claim: Al-Zajjaj explains the feminine singular ukh rā despite plural maʾārib by treating the plural as a collective, as if the phrase said ‘a group of other needs.’
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p279/r5.anchor: فان قيل المآرب جمع فكيف قال أخرى ولم يقل اخر فالجواب أن المآرب في معنى جماعة فكأنه قال جماعة من الحاجات أخرى قاله الزجاج

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p278#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p278#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p278#2/r4.claim: Moses leans on the staff while walking.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p278#2/r4.anchor: أتوكأ عليها} أي: أعتمد عليها في حال المشي

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p278#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p278#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p278#2/r5.claim: Moses shakes branches with the staff so leaves fall for his sheep to eat.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p278#2/r5.anchor: وأهش بها على غنمي} أي: أهز بها الشجرة ليسقط ورقها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p278#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p278#2/r6.speaker: مالك
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p278#2/r6.claim: Malik defines hashsh as placing the hooked staff in a branch and shaking leaves and fruit down without breaking the branch, unlike striking it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p278#2/r6.anchor: عبد الرحمن بن القاسم: عن الإمام مالك: والهش: أن يضع الرجل المحجن

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p278#2/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p278#2/r7.speaker: ميمون بن مهران
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p278#2/r7.claim: Maymun ibn Mihran gives the same explanation of gently shaking a branch to drop its leaves and fruit.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p278#2/r7.anchor: ولا يكسر العود، فهذا الهش، ولا يخبط. وكذا قال ميمون بن مهران أيضا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p279/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p279/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p279/r1.claim: Musa's staff served other interests, benefits, and needs besides those he has just named.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p279/r1.anchor: {ولي فيها مآرب أخرى} أي: مصالح ومنافع وحاجات أخر غير ذلك

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p279/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p279/r2.speaker: بعضهم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p279/r2.claim: Some commentators list extraordinary supposed uses: lighting at night, guarding the flock while Moses slept, and growing into a shade tree.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p279/r2.anchor: فقيل: كانت تضيء له بالليل، وتحرس له الغنم إذا نام، ويغرسها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p279/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p279/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p279/r3.claim: Ibn Kathir rejects those extraordinary details as apparent Israeli reports: if the staff had such powers, Moses would not have fled when it became a serpent.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p279/r3.anchor: والظاهر أنها لم تكن كذلك، ولو كانت كذلك لما استنكر موسى صيرورتها ثعبانا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p279/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p279/r4.speaker: بعضهم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p279/r4.claim: One reported claim says the staff had belonged to Adam; Ibn Kathir groups such stories with Israeli reports.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p279/r4.anchor: وكذا قول بعضهم: إنها كانت لآدم، عليه السلام

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p279/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p279/r5.speaker: الآخر
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p279/r5.claim: Another reported claim identifies the staff as the beast that will emerge before the Day of Resurrection; Ibn Kathir treats such claims as Israeli reports.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p279/r5.anchor: وقول الآخر: إنها هي الدابة التي تخرج قبل يوم القيامة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p279/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p279/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p279/r6.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas gives the staff the name Masha.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p279/r6.anchor: وروي عن ابن عباس أنه قال: كان اسمها ماشا

JISHUMI:v6p4648/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4648/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4648/r4.claim: Some say God asked about the staff's uses; after Moses mentioned one use, God indicated further uses, including its role in miracles.
JISHUMI:v6p4648/r4.anchor: وقيل: أراد أن يسأله عن منافع العصا، فلما بين بعضه أخبر أن فيه منافع أخر ككونه معجزة له

JISHUMI:v6p4648/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4648/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4648/r5.claim: Another explanation takes the question as asking about the staff's uses, like asking about Dhū al-Qarnayn to elicit his story.
JISHUMI:v6p4648/r5.anchor: وقيل إنما سأله عن منافع العصا فلذلك أجاب بالمنافع كقوله: (ويسألونك عن ذي القرنين) أي: عن قصته.

JISHUMI:v6p4648/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4648/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4648/r6.claim: The staff reportedly had two forks and a pair of points at its base; it was said to come from a myrtle tree in Paradise, brought by Adam and passed down to Shuʿayb, who gave it to Moses.
JISHUMI:v6p4648/r6.anchor: وكانت لها شعبتان وفي أسفلها سنان، وقيل: كانت من آس الجنة أخرجها آدم - عليه السلام - وتوارثوها

JISHUMI:v6p4648/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4648/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4648/r7.claim: Moses leaned on the staff for support while walking or when tired.
JISHUMI:v6p4648/r7.anchor: أعتمد عليها إذا مشيت أو أعييت

JISHUMI:v6p4648/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4648/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4648/r8.claim: He shook leaves from trees so his sheep could eat them.
JISHUMI:v6p4648/r8.anchor: أخبط بها ورق الأشجار لترعاه غنمي.

JISHUMI:v6p4648/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4648/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4648/r9.claim: Moses used the plural أخر rather than أخرَيات to fit the verse endings.

JISHUMI:v6p4648/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4648/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
JISHUMI:v6p4648/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās lists many staff uses: carrying provisions, drawing water or food from the ground, guarding sheep, fighting enemies, serving as a bucket, providing a light, talking to Moses, and reaching desired fruit.
JISHUMI:v6p4648/r10.anchor: قال ابن عباس: كان يحمل عليها زاده، ويكزها فيخرج الماء، ويضرب الأرض فيخرج ما يأكل، وكان يقي بها غنمه من السباع

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p59/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p59/r3.speaker: ابن أبي إسحاق
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p59/r3.claim: Ibn Abī Isḥāq reads عصي, following Hudhayl's treatment of the final alif before yāʾ of the first-person suffix, with 12:19 cited as a parallel.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p59/r3.anchor: قرأ ابن أبي إسحاق ( عصي ) على لغة هذيل . ومثله { الرياح بشرى }

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p59/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p59/r4.speaker: الحسن
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p59/r4.claim: Al-Ḥasan reads عصاي with a kasra on the yāʾ to meet the two sukūns, like 14:22; Ibn Abī Isḥāq is also reported to read the yāʾ without a vowel.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p59/r4.anchor: وقرأ الحسن ( عصاي ) بكسر الياء لالتقاء الساكنين ، وهو مثل قراءة حمزة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p59/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p59/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p59/r5.claim: Mūsā leans on the staff when tired or stopped at the head of the flock, and when leaping.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p59/r5.anchor: أعتمد عليها إذا أعييت أو وقفت على رأس القطيع وعند الطفرة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p59/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p59/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p59/r6.claim: هش الورق means striking or shaking leaves down for the sheep to eat; a saying attributed to Luqmān ibn ʿĀd uses هشة for a brittle twig, and نخب is a valley near Ṭāʾif.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p59/r6.anchor: هش الورق : خبطه أي : أخبطه على رؤس غنمي تأكله

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p59/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p59/r7.speaker: النخعي
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p59/r7.claim: Al-Nakhaʿī reads أهش; the author relates both forms to هش الخبز, bread breaking because it is brittle.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p59/r7.anchor: وفي قراءة النخعي : أهش ، وكلاهما من هش الخبز يهش

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p59/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p59/r8.speaker: عكرمة
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p59/r8.claim: ʿIkrima reads أهس with sīn, meaning that Mūsā drove the sheep with a call; الهس is the driving of sheep.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p59/r8.anchor: وعن عكرمة : أهس بالسين ، أي : أنحى عليها زاجرا لها . والهس : زجر الغنم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p59/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p59/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p59/r9.claim: Mūsā lists the staff's familiar uses in detail and summary as though sensing a great event to come, explaining it is ordinarily useful only like other sticks; alternatively, God elicits its many uses before revealing the far greater miracle.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p59/r9.anchor: ذكر على التفصيل والإجمال المنافع المتعلقة بالعصا ، كأنه أحس بما يعقب هذا السؤال من أمر عظيم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p59/r11.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p59/r11.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p59/r11.claim: Some say Mūsā gave a summary so God would ask about the uses and thereby honor him with further conversation.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p59/r11.anchor: وقالوا : إنما أجمل موسى ليسأله عن تلك المآرب فيزيد في إكرامه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p59/r12.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p59/r12.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p59/r12.claim: Some say awe made Mūsā lose his speech and answer only in summary.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p59/r13.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p59/r13.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p59/r13.claim: One report names the staff's wood as nabʿa.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p59/r14.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p59/r14.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p59/r14.claim: A report lists extra staff functions: hooks and forks to gather branches or break them, carry gear, make shade, extend a short rope, and defend the flock from predators.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p59/r14.anchor: كانت ذات شعبتين ومحجن ، فإذا طال الغصن حناه بالمحجن

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p59/r15.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p59/r15.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p59/r15.claim: Another report gives miraculous functions: drawing water by lengthening and becoming a bucket, lighting the night, fighting enemies, producing fruit or water, following Mūsā while carrying supplies, and protecting him from vermin.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p59/r15.anchor: كان فيها من المعجزات أنه كان يستقي بها فتطول بطول البئر وتصير شعبتاها دلوا

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p398/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p398/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p398/r2.claim: Moses's answer that it is a staff would suffice; saying it is his adds the fact of ownership.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p398/r2.anchor: فتضمن جوابه أمرين : أحدهما : الإخبار بأنها عصا وهذا جواب كاف . الثاني : إضافتها إلى ملكه

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p398/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p398/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p398/r3.claim: Moses mentions uses he was not asked about to show his reliance on the staff, not that he carries it idly.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p398/r3.anchor: ثم أخبر عن حالها بما لم يسأل عنه ليوضح شدة حاجته إليها واستعانته بها لئلا يكون عابئا بحملها

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p398/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p398/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p398/r4.claim: “I lean on it” describes using the staff for support.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p398/r4.anchor: وأهش به على غنمي } أي أخبط بها ورق الشجر لترعاه غنمي

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p398/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p398/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p398/r5.claim: To “hush” with the staff is to knock leaves from trees for the sheep to eat.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p398/r5.anchor: أي أخبط بها ورق الشجر لترعاه غنمي

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p398/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p398/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p398/r6.claim: A rajaz line uses “ahush” for knocking leaves from trees for sheep; the poem is the author's linguistic evidence.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p398/r6.anchor: أهش بالعصا على أغنامي … من ناعم الأراك والبشام

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p398/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p398/r7.speaker: عكرمة
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p398/r7.claim: Ikrima reads the word with an unpointed sīn: “wa-ahussu.”
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p398/r7.anchor: وقرأ عكرمة ( وأهس ) بسين غير معجمة

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p398/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p398/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p398/r8.claim: One view treats “hashsh” and “hass” as two dialect forms with the same meaning.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p398/r8.anchor: وفي الهش والهس وجهان : أحدهما : أنهما لغتان معناهما واحد

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p398/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p398/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p398/r9.claim: A second view distinguishes them: hashsh is striking leaves from trees, while hass is driving the sheep.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p398/r9.anchor: والثاني : أن معناهما مختلف , فالهش بالمعجمة : خبط الشجر , والهس بغير إعجام زجر الغنم

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p398/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p398/r10.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p398/r10.claim: “Other needs” names necessary uses of the staff while alluding to incidental ones.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p398/r10.anchor: أي حاجات أخرى , فنص على اللازم وكنى عن العارض

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p398/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p398/r11.speaker: مقاتل
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p398/r11.claim: One additional use was driving away predators.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p398/r11.anchor: أحدها : أنه كان يطرد بها السباع , قاله مقاتل

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p398/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p398/r12.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p398/r12.claim: Other reported uses were kindling fire and drawing water.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p398/r12.anchor: الثاني : أنه كان يقدح بها النار , ويستخرج الماء بها

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p398/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p398/r13.speaker: الضحاك
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p398/r13.claim: Al-Dahhak says the staff illuminated the way for Moses at night.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p398/r13.anchor: الثالث : أنها كانت تضيء له بالليل , قاله الضحاك

MUQATIL:20:17-18/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:17-18/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:17-18/r2.claim: Moses leaned on the staff for support while walking.

MUQATIL:20:17-18/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:17-18/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:17-18/r3.claim: He struck trees so leaves fell for his young flock to eat.

MUQATIL:20:17-18/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:17-18/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:17-18/r4.claim: Other uses included carrying provisions and a waterskin, producing food and water, shining at night, turning the flock back, protecting it, and killing snakes and scorpions by God's permission.
MUQATIL:20:17-18/r4.anchor: وكان موسى، عليه السلام، يحمل زاده وسقاءه على عصاه

MUQATIL:20:17-18/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:17-18/r5.speaker: مقاتل
MUQATIL:20:17-18/r5.claim: Muqatil reports that Gabriel gave Moses the staff at night as he headed to Midian; its name was Nafa.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p52#4/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p52#4/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p52#4/r1.claim: Moses leaned on the staff when tired, when standing at the head of the flock, and when leaping.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p52#4/r1.anchor: اعتمد عليها إذا أعييت أو وقفت على رأس القطيع وعند الطفرة

NASAFI-FULL:v3p52#4/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p52#4/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p52#4/r2.claim: He shook tree branches with it so their leaves would fall for his sheep to eat.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p52#4/r2.anchor: أخبط ورق الشجر على غنمي لتأكل

NASAFI-FULL:v3p52#4/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p52#4/r3.speaker: حفص
NASAFI-FULL:v3p52#4/r3.claim: The text identifies Ḥafṣ's reading at wa-lī fīhā.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p52#4/r3.anchor: ﴿ ولي فيها ﴾ حفص ﴿ مآرب ﴾ جمع مأربة

NASAFI-FULL:v3p52#4/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p52#4/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p52#4/r4.claim: Maʾārib is the plural of maʾriba, which has three possible vowelings and means needs.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p52#4/r4.anchor: جمع مأربة بالحركات الثلاثة وهي بالحاجة

NASAFI-FULL:v3p52#4/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p52#4/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p52#4/r5.claim: The feminine ukhrā differs from the expected masculine ukhar because it refers to a plural collective or matches the verse endings, as with al-kubrā.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p52#4/r5.anchor: والقياس اخر وإنما قال أخرى ردا إلى الجماعة أو لنسق الآي وكذا الكبرى

NASAFI-FULL:v3p52#4/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p52#4/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p52#4/r6.claim: The staff also walked and spoke with him, fought enemies and beasts, became a well rope and bucket, gave light, carried provisions, grew fruit, brought water, and warded off vermin.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p52#4/r6.anchor: والمآرب الآخر أنها كانت تماشيه وتحدثه وتحارب العدو والسباع وتصير رشاء فتطول بطول البئر

NASAFI-FULL:v3p52#4/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p52#4/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p52#4/r7.claim: His added details either express gratitude while he mentions some benefits and modestly leaves the rest, or answer an implied second question about what he does with the staff.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p52#4/r7.anchor: والزيادة على الجواب لتعداد النعم شكرا أو لأنها جواب سؤال آخر لأنه لما قال هي عصاي قيل له ما تصنع بها

QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18/r6.speaker: ابن الجوهري
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18/r6.claim: Ibn al-Jawharī cites a report that God reproached Moses for attributing the staff to himself, then told him to cast it down so he would see that he did not own or control it.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18/r6.anchor: وقال ابن الجوهري: وفي بعض الآثار أن الله تعالى عتب على موسى إضافة العصا إلى نفسه في ذلك الموطن

QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18/r7.speaker: ابن أبي إسحاق
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18/r7.claim: Ibn Abī Isḥāq reads عصي according to Hudhayl usage, like يا بشري and محيي.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18/r7.anchor: وقرأ ابن أبي إسحاق «عصي» على لغة هذيل ومثله «يا بشري» و«محيي»

QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18/r8.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18/r8.claim: Al-Ḥasan reads عصاي with kasra on the yāʾ to avoid two adjacent quiescent letters, like Ḥamza’s بمصرخي in 14:22; Ibn Abī Isḥāq is also reported to use a still yāʾ.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18/r8.anchor: وقرأ الحسن «عصاي» بكسر الياء لالتقاء الساكنين. ومثل هذا قراءة حمزة: ومآ أنتم بمصرخي [إبراهيم: 22].

QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18/r9.claim: Moses answers with four details beyond the question: ownership, leaning on the staff, shaking leaves, and his many other uses; the author compares this fuller answer to Prophetic answers about seawater and a child’s pilgrimage.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18/r9.anchor: في هذه الآية دليل على جواب السؤال بأكثر مما سئل لأنه لما قال: { وما تلك بيمينك يموسى } ذكر معاني أربعة

QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18/r10.claim: To lean on the staff means to support oneself while walking or standing.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18/r10.anchor: قوله تعالى: { أتوكأ عليها } أي أتحامل عليها في المشي والوقوف ومنه الاتكاء.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18/r11.speaker: النخعي
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18/r11.claim: Al-Nakhaʿī reads وأهش with shīn; it means beating tree branches so leaves fall for the sheep to eat.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18/r11.anchor: «وأهش» أيضا ذكره النحاس. وهي قراءة النخعي، أي أخبط بها الورق، أي أضرب أغصان الشجر

QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#2/r1.claim: The staff shakes leaves from tree branches so the sheep can eat them easily.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#2/r1.anchor: أهش بالعصا على أغنامي من ناعم الأراك والبشام

QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#2/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#2/r2.claim: A rajaz verse uses أهش for shaking branches with a staff to provide leaves for sheep.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#2/r2.anchor: أهش بالعصا على أغنامي من ناعم الأراك والبشام

QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#2/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#2/r3.claim: هش على غنمه has a future verb with ḍamma on hāʾ, whereas هش إلى الرجل and هش للمعروف use fatḥa; the source also cites Umar’s expression هششت.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#2/r3.anchor: يقال: هش على غنمه يهش بضم الهاء في المستقبل. وهش إلى الرجل يهش بالفتح. وكذلك هش للمعروف يهش

QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#2/r4.speaker: شمر
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#2/r4.claim: Shammar explains the saying about ʿUmar as meaning that he became joyful and desirous; هاش can also mean هش.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#2/r4.anchor: وفي حديث عمر: هششت يوما فقبلت وأنا صائم. قال شمر: أي فرحت واشتهيت. قال: ويجوز هاش بمعنى هش.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#2/r5.speaker: الراعي
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#2/r5.claim: Al-Rāʿī’s verse uses هاش فؤاده to mean that his heart rejoiced or was excited; the root sense is softness.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#2/r5.anchor: قال الراعي: فكبر للرويا وهاش فؤاده وبشر نفسا كان قبل يلومها أي طرب. والأصل في الكلمة الرخاوة.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#2/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#2/r6.claim: The root also describes a soft man or a soft spouse.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#2/r6.anchor: والأصل في الكلمة الرخاوة. يقال: رجل هش وزوج هش.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#2/r7.speaker: عكرمة
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#2/r7.claim: ʿIkrima reads وأهس with an unmarked sīn; some treat it as synonymous with the shīn reading, while others distinguish beating branches from driving or shooing sheep.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#2/r7.anchor: وقرأ عكرمة «وأهس» بالسين غير معجمة قيل: هما لغتان بمعنى واحد.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#2/r8.speaker: الماوردي والزمخشري
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#2/r8.claim: Al-Māwardī and al-Zamakhsharī distinguish the readings: shīn means striking branches, while sīn means shooing sheep; ʿIkrima’s form means driving them onward.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#2/r8.anchor: زجر الغنم ذكره الماوردي وكذلك ذكر الزمخشري.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#2/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#2/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#2/r9.claim: مآرب means needs or uses; its singular is مأربة, مأربة, or مأربة with different vocalizations.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#2/r9.anchor: الرابعة: قوله تعالى { ولي فيها مآرب أخرى } أي حوائج. واحدها مأربة ومأربة ومأربة.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#2/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#2/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#2/r10.claim: أخرى is singular because nonhuman plurals are commonly treated as feminine singular in modifiers and pronouns, as in 7:180 and 34:10.
