QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#2/r10.anchor: وقال «أخرى» على صيغة الواحد لأن مآرب في معنى الجماعة، لكن المهيع في توابع جمع ما لا يعقل الإفراد

QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#3/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#3/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās lists the staff’s uses: lengthening a short well-rope, making shade, killing vermin, carrying gear, and defending sheep from predators.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#3/r1.anchor: تعرض قوم لتعديد منافع العصا منهم ابن عباس، قال: إذا انتهيت إلى رأس بئر فقصر الرشا وصلته بالعصا

QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#3/r2.speaker: ميمون بن مهران
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#3/r2.claim: Maymūn ibn Mihrān reports from Ibn ʿAbbās that holding a staff is a prophetic sunnah and a sign of the believer.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#3/r2.anchor: وروى عنه ميمون بن مهران قال: إمساك العصا سنة للأنبياء، وعلامة للمؤمن.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#3/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#3/r3.speaker: الحسن البصري
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#3/r3.claim: Al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī assigns six benefits to the staff: prophetic practice, righteous adornment, weapon against enemies, aid to the weak, distress to hypocrites, and increased obedience.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#3/r3.anchor: وقال الحسن البصري: فيها ست خصال سنة للأنبياء، وزينة الصلحاء، وسلاح على الأعداء، وعون للضعفاء

QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#3/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#3/r4.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#3/r4.claim: A saying holds that a believer’s staff frightens away Satan and humbles hypocrites and sinners, and serves as a prayer direction and strength when tired.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#3/r4.anchor: ويقال: إذا كان مع المؤمن العصا يهرب منه الشيطان، ويخشع منه المنافق والفاجر، وتكون قبلته إذا صلى

QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#3/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#3/r5.speaker: أعرابي
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#3/r5.claim: A Bedouin tells al-Ḥajjāj that his staff supports prayer and travel, helps him walk, cross streams, avoid falls, find shade and warmth, carry gear, defend himself and animals, and substitute for spear or sword; it is inherited and shakes leaves for sheep.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#3/r5.anchor: لقى الحجاج أعرابيا فقال: من أين أقبلت يا أعرابي؟ قال: من البادية. قال: وما في يدك؟ قال: عصاي أركزها لصلاتي

QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#3/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#3/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#3/r6.claim: Staffs serve in religious practice, including as a prayer barrier in open country; the Prophet used a small spear and had a lance planted before him for Eid prayers, established in authentic reports.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#3/r6.anchor: قلت: منافع العصا كثيرة، ولها مدخل في مواضع من الشريعة: منها تتخذ قبلة في الصحراء وقد كان للنبي عليه الصلاة والسلام

QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#3/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#3/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#3/r7.claim: The spear, small lance, and related weapon names denote the same object.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#3/r7.anchor: والحربة والعنزة والنيزك والآلة أسماء لمسمى واحد.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#3/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#3/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#3/r8.claim: An authentic report says the Prophet had a crooked staff with which he indicated a stone he could not reach to kiss.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#3/r8.anchor: وكان له محجن وهو عصا معوجة الطرف يشير به إلى الحجر إذا لم يستطع أن يقبله ثابت في الصحيح أيضا.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#3/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#3/r9.speaker: السائب بن يزيد
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#3/r9.claim: In al-Muwaṭṭaʾ, al-Sāʾib ibn Yazīd reports that ʿUmar assigned Ubayy ibn Kaʿb and Tamīm al-Dārī to lead eleven rakʿas; people leaned on staffs through long recitation until dawn.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#3/r9.anchor: وفي الموطأ عن السائب بن يزيد أنه قال: أمر عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه أبي بن كعب وتميما الداري

QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#4/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#4/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#4/r1.claim: The two Ṣaḥīḥ collections report that the Prophet had a walking stick.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#4/r1.anchor: وفي الصحيحين: أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام كان له مخصرة.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#4/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#4/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#4/r2.claim: There is consensus that a preacher may lean on a sword or staff; the author calls the staff’s origin noble and says only the ignorant deny it.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#4/r2.anchor: والإجماع منعقد على أن الخطيب يخطب متوكئا على سيف أو عصا، فالعصا مأخوذة من أصل كريم

QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#4/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#4/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#4/r3.claim: Moses’ staff gathered mighty signs and proofs through which the resistant magicians believed.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#4/r3.anchor: وقد جمع الله لموسى في عصاه من البراهين العظام، والآيات الجسام، ما آمن به السحرة المعاندون.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#4/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#4/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#4/r4.claim: Solomon used a staff for sermons, exhortation, and lengthy prayer.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#4/r4.anchor: واتخذها سليمان لخطبته وموعظته وطول صلاته.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#4/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#4/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#4/r5.claim: Ibn Masʿūd kept the Prophet’s staff and small spear and preached with a rod; caliphs and leading preachers also used staffs, illustrating their honored status.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#4/r5.anchor: وكان ابن مسعود صاحب عصا النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وعنزته وكان يخطب بالقضيب وكفى بذلك فضلا على شرف حال العصا

QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#4/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#4/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#4/r6.claim: Arab eloquent speakers traditionally took and leaned on staffs and gestured with them in conversation, assemblies, and sermons.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#4/r6.anchor: وعادة العرب العرباء، الفصحاء اللسن البلغاء أخذ المخصرة والعصا والاعتماد عليها عند الكلام، وفي المحافل والخطب.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#4/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#4/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#4/r7.claim: The Shuʿūbiyya criticized Arab preachers for carrying and gesturing with staffs; the author says they despise Arabs and prefer non-Arabs.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#4/r7.anchor: وأنكرت الشعوبية على خطباء العرب أخذ المخصرة والإشارة بها إلى المعاني. والشعوبية تبغض العرب وتفضل العجم.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#4/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#4/r8.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#4/r8.claim: Mālik says ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib held a staff for support, as older men need it when standing more than young men.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#4/r8.anchor: قال مالك: كان عطاء ابن السائب يمسك المخصرة يستعين بها. قال مالك: والرجل إذا كبر لم يكن مثل الشباب يقوى بها عند قيامه.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#4/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#4/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#4/r9.claim: An anonymous poet jokes that he once walked on two legs supported by a staff but now walks on another wooden leg.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#4/r9.anchor: قد كنت أمشي على رجلين معتمدا فصرت أمشي على أخرى من الخشب

QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#4/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#4/r10.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#4/r10.claim: Mālik says people went out in rain with staffs for support, even young men; Rabīʿa might take a seated visitor’s staff until he stood.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#4/r10.anchor: قال مالك رحمه الله ورضي عنه: وقد كان الناس إذا جاءهم المطر خرجوا بالعصي يتوكأون عليها، حتى لقد كان الشباب يحبسون عصيهم

QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#4/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#4/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#4/r11.claim: The author includes correcting one’s wives with a staff among its uses, claiming this can improve them and their relationship with him.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#4/r11.anchor: ومن منافع العصا ضرب الرجل نساءه بها فيما يصلحهم، ويصلح حاله وحالهم معه.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#4/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#4/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#4/r12.claim: One Prophetic report says Abū Jahm never puts his staff down from his shoulder.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#4/r12.anchor: وأما أبو جهم فلا يضع عصاه عن عاتقه

QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#4/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#4/r13.speaker: عبادة بن الصامت
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#4/r13.claim: A report from ʿUbāda ibn al-Ṣāmit, recorded by al-Nasāʾī, quotes the Prophet advising a man not to put down his staff from his family, to make them fear God.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#4/r13.anchor: لا ترفع عصاك عن أهلك أخفهم في الله " رواه عبادة بن الصامت خرجه النسائي.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#4/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#4/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#4/r14.claim: Another Prophetic saying advises hanging a whip where one’s family can see it; the author says this was discussed earlier under al-Nisāʾ.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#4/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#4/r15.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#4/r15.claim: Carrying a staff can remind a person that this world is temporary and life a journey; an ascetic said he carried one because it is travel equipment.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#4/r15.anchor: ومن فوائدها التنبيه على الانتقال من هذه الدار كما قيل لبعض الزهاد: ما لك تمشي على عصا ولست بكبير ولا مريض؟

QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#5/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#5/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#5/r1.claim: The poem says the speaker carries a staff by choice, not weakness or age, to teach himself that a resident here is still on a journey.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18#5/r1.anchor: حملت العصا لا الضعف أوجب حملها علي ولا أني تحنيت من كبر ولكنني ألزمت نفسي حملها لأعلمها أن المقيم على سفر

QASHANI:20:17-18/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:20:17-18/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:20:17-18/r2.claim: The staff represents reliance on intellect in the visible world, acquiring perfection, journeying to God, and taking on divine traits; these require it.
QASHANI:20:17-18/r2.anchor: أعتمد في عالم الشهادة وكسب الكمال والسير إلى الله والتخلق بأخلاقه عليها

QASHANI:20:17-18/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:20:17-18/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:20:17-18/r3.claim: Moses shakes useful sciences and practical wisdom from the tree of spirit by thought, feeding the animal faculties represented by his flock.
QASHANI:20:17-18/r3.anchor: أخبط أوراق العلوم النافعة والحكم العملية من شجرة الروح بحركة الفكر بها على غنم القوى الحيوانية

QASHANI:20:17-18/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:20:17-18/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:20:17-18/r4.claim: The staff also serves the acquisition of spiritual stations and the pursuit of states, gifts, and disclosures.
QASHANI:20:17-18/r4.anchor: من كسب المقامات وطلب الأحوال والمواهب والتجليات

QASHANI:20:17-18/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:20:17-18/r6.speaker: author
QASHANI:20:17-18/r6.claim: Moses' answer exceeds the question because of his intense longing for conversation and sustained delight in intimacy.
QASHANI:20:17-18/r6.anchor: وإنما زاد الجواب على السؤال لشدة شغفه بالمكالمة واستدامة ذوق الاستئناس

RAZI-FULL:v22p22#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p22#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p22#2/r2.claim: God asks about the staff's uses so Moses names some and then learns it has greater uses than he knew, showing that human reason cannot know all the properties of even a present object without divine guidance.
RAZI-FULL:v22p22#2/r2.anchor: فسأله عن منافع العصا فذكر بعضها فعرفه الله تعالى أن فيها منافع أعظم مما ذكر

RAZI-FULL:v22p23/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p23/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p23/r4.claim: Naming the staff and its benefits suggests a heart occupied by created things; Razi contrasts this with Muhammad’s undistracted vision of Paradise and Hell.
RAZI-FULL:v22p23/r4.anchor: فذكر العصا ومن كان قلبه مشغولا بالعصا ومنافعها كيف يكون مستغرقا في بحر معرفة الحق

RAZI-FULL:v22p23/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p23/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v22p23/r5.claim: Razi cites Muhammad’s response to being asked to praise God: he cannot enumerate the praise, and God is as He praised Himself; no grading is stated.
RAZI-FULL:v22p23/r5.anchor: ولكن محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم عرض عليه الجنة والنار

RAZI-FULL:v22p23/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p23/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p23/r6.claim: The staff becoming a serpent teaches that attention to anything besides God is a distracting danger, like a lethal serpent; Razi links this to Abraham’s disavowal of false gods.
RAZI-FULL:v22p23/r6.anchor: ليعرف أن كل ما سوى الله فالالتفات إليه شاغل وهو كالحية المهلكة لك

RAZI-FULL:v22p23/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p23/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p23/r7.claim: Razi cites a hadith that unpaid zakat wealth will come on Judgment Day in the form of a bald serpent; he gives no chain or grading.
RAZI-FULL:v22p23/r7.anchor: يجاء يوم القيامة بصاحب المال الذي لم يؤد زكاته

RAZI-FULL:v22p23/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p23/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p23/r8.claim: Moses had already answered by identifying the staff, but listed more uses as a means to prolong his conversation with God, which he loved.
RAZI-FULL:v22p23/r8.anchor: وثالثها : أنه قال هي عصاي فقد تم الجواب

RAZI-FULL:v22p23/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p23/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p23/r9.claim: اتوكأ means to lean on the staff when tired, pausing by the flock, or crossing a leap; التوكي and الاتكاء are compared with التوقي and الاتقاء.
RAZI-FULL:v22p23/r9.anchor: والتوكي ، والإتكاء ، واحد كالتوقي ، والإتقاء معناه اعتمد عليها إذا عييت

RAZI-FULL:v22p23/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p23/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p23/r10.claim: Razi contrasts Moses leaning on a staff with Muhammad relying on God’s mercy, citing divine sufficiency and protection for the Prophet.
RAZI-FULL:v22p23/r10.anchor: وقال الله تعالى لمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( اتكىء على رحمتي ) بقوله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v22p23/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p23/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p23/r11.claim: In 8:64, ومن اتبعك is coordinated with the pronoun in حسبك الله, so the meaning is that God suffices both Muhammad and the believers who follow him.
RAZI-FULL:v22p23/r11.anchor: معطوف على الكاف في قوله : { حسبك الله } والمعنى الله حسبك

RAZI-FULL:v22p23#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p23#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p23#2/r1.claim: Moses shakes or strikes tree branches with the staff so leaves fall for his sheep to eat.
RAZI-FULL:v22p23#2/r1.anchor: أي أخبط بها فأضرب أغصان الشجر ليسقط ورقها على غنمي فتأكله

RAZI-FULL:v22p23#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p23#2/r2.speaker: ثعلب
RAZI-FULL:v22p23#2/r2.claim: Thaʿlab distinguishes the verb’s vowel in expressions for shaking sheep, striking a man, and bread crumbling.
RAZI-FULL:v22p23#2/r2.anchor: هش الرغيف يهش بكسر الهاء . قاله ثعلب

RAZI-FULL:v22p23#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p23#2/r3.speaker: عكرمة
RAZI-FULL:v22p23#2/r3.claim: ʿIkrima reads وأهس with an unpointed sīn; Razi explains this form as driving or shooing sheep.
RAZI-FULL:v22p23#2/r3.anchor: وقرأ عكرمة : ( وأهس ) بالسين غير المنقوطة

RAZI-FULL:v22p23#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p23#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p23#2/r4.claim: Moses mentions his own needs before the flock, his dependents; Razi contrasts this with Muhammad’s concern for his community in life and at the Resurrection.

RAZI-FULL:v22p23#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p23#2/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v22p23#2/r5.claim: Razi cites Muhammad praying, “O God, guide my people, for they do not know”; no grading is stated.
RAZI-FULL:v22p23#2/r5.anchor: اللهم اهد قومي فإنهم لا يعلمون

RAZI-FULL:v22p23#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p23#2/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v22p23#2/r6.claim: Razi says Muhammad will put his community first at the Resurrection, saying “My community, my community”; no grading is stated.
RAZI-FULL:v22p23#2/r6.anchor: ومحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم لم يشتغل في الدنيا إلا بإصلاح أمر الأمة

RAZI-FULL:v22p23#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p23#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p23#2/r7.claim: مآرب means needs or benefits; its singular is مأربة, with the rāʾ read in more than one way.
RAZI-FULL:v22p23#2/r7.anchor: أي حوائج ومنافع واحدتها مأربة بفتح الراء وضمها

RAZI-FULL:v22p23#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p23#2/r8.speaker: ابن الأعرابي وقطرب
RAZI-FULL:v22p23#2/r8.claim: Ibn al-Aʿrābī and Quṭrub also report مأربة with kasra; الأرب and الإربة likewise mean a need.
RAZI-FULL:v22p23#2/r8.anchor: وحكى ابن الأعرابي وقطرب بكسر الراء أيضا

RAZI-FULL:v22p23#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p23#2/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p23#2/r9.claim: أخرى is feminine because مآرب conveys a collective group; أخر would also be correct, as in 2:184.

RAZI-FULL:v22p23#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p23#2/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p23#2/r10.claim: Moses states what he knows about the staff’s uses and summarizes the other, as yet unknown, purposes because God’s question signals hidden significance.
RAZI-FULL:v22p23#2/r10.anchor: عرف أن لله فيه أسرارا عظيمة فذكر ما عرف وعبر عن البواقي التي ما عرفها إجمالا

RAZI-FULL:v22p23#2/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p23#2/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p23#2/r11.claim: Moses presents the staff as ordinary, yet recognizes that God’s asking about it means it has further benefits, including occasioning God’s speech to him.
RAZI-FULL:v22p23#2/r11.anchor: إلهي ما هذه العصا إلا كغيرها ، لكنك لما سألت عنها عرفت أن لي فيها مآرب أخرى

RAZI-FULL:v22p23#2/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p23#2/r12.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p23#2/r12.claim: Moses generalizes about other uses in hope that God will ask about them, allowing their conversation to continue.
RAZI-FULL:v22p23#2/r12.anchor: أجمل رجاء أن يسأل ربه عن تلك المآرب فيسمع كلام الله مرة أخرى

RAZI-FULL:v22p23#2/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p23#2/r13.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p23#2/r13.claim: By divine gentleness Moses began speaking, then awe overwhelmed and confused him, so he again gave a general answer.
RAZI-FULL:v22p23#2/r13.anchor: بسبب اللطف انطلق لسانه ثم غلبته الدهشة فانقطع لسانه وتشوش فكره

RAZI-FULL:v22p23#2/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p23#2/r14.speaker: وهب
RAZI-FULL:v22p23#2/r14.claim: Wahb describes the staff as forked like a crook: it hooked or twisted branches, carried Moses’ gear, and could be planted with his cloak to make shade.
RAZI-FULL:v22p23#2/r14.anchor: ثم قال وهب : كانت ذات شعبتين كالمحجن ، فإذا طال الغصن حناه بالمحجن

QUSHAYRI:v2p256/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p256/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p256/r2.claim: The first step on the path is to abandon every means and strip away every pursuit, so Moses’ listing of uses for the staff raises a question about reliance on it.
QUSHAYRI:v2p256/r2.anchor: أول قدم في الطريق ترك كل سبب ، والتنقي عن كل طلب

QUSHAYRI:v2p256/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p256/r3.speaker: ويقال
QUSHAYRI:v2p256/r3.claim: Another reading says that the more Moses detailed the staff’s uses, the more firmly he should trust God enough to cast it aside.
QUSHAYRI:v2p256/r3.anchor: تفصيلا في انتفاعه بعصاه إلا كان أقوى وأولى بأن يؤمن بإلقائها

QUSHAYRI:v2p256/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p256/r7.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p256/r7.claim: Overjoyed by God’s speech, Moses answered both the question asked and the question unasked, listing the staff’s benefits.
QUSHAYRI:v2p256/r7.anchor: ويقال لما باسطه الحق بسماع كلامه أخذته أريحية سماع الخطاب

QUSHAYRI:v2p256/r8.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p256/r8.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p256/r8.claim: Moses lists that the staff keeps him company alone, lights the dark, carries him when tired, helps him tend sheep, and repels enemies.
QUSHAYRI:v2p256/r8.anchor: وذكر وجوها من الانتفاع ؛ منها أنه قال تؤنسني في حال وحدتي

QUSHAYRI:v2p256/r10.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p256/r10.speaker: ويقال
QUSHAYRI:v2p256/r10.claim: Another reading says the staff had an unlisted benefit: its becoming a serpent was a miracle and proof of Moses’ truthfulness.
QUSHAYRI:v2p256/r10.anchor: قال الحق - بعد ما عدد موسى وجوه الآيات

QUSHAYRI:v2p256/r11.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p256/r11.speaker: ويقال
QUSHAYRI:v2p256/r11.claim: All the staff’s benefits came from God, so Moses should not attribute them to himself; a poem makes the same point about gifts given to the beloved.
QUSHAYRI:v2p256/r11.anchor: ويقال جميع ما عدد من المنافع في العصا كان من قبل الله

QUSHAYRI:v2p256/r12.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p256/r12.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p256/r12.claim: Poetry says that when gifts are given to you, none of them is truly from you.
QUSHAYRI:v2p256/r12.anchor: يا جنة الخلد ، والهدايا إذا . . . تهدى إليك فما منك يهدى

STUDYQURAN:20:17/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:17/r2.speaker: al-Rāzī
STUDYQURAN:20:17/r2.claim: Al-Rāzī explains that God is making Moses recognize the reality of a piece of wood that can neither harm nor benefit but will become a mighty serpent.
STUDYQURAN:20:17/r2.anchor: Al-Rāzī explains it this way: “It is as if God said, ‘O Moses, do you know the reality of that which is in your hand

STUDYQURAN:20:17/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:17/r3.speaker: traditional Islamic lore
STUDYQURAN:20:17/r3.claim: Traditional lore says the staff belonged first to Adam, came from a pillar in Heaven, passed prophet to prophet to Shuʿayb, and was given to Moses at his marriage to Shuʿayb's daughter.
STUDYQURAN:20:17/r3.anchor: In traditional Islamic lore, the staff of Moses is said to have belonged initially to Adam and was made from a pillar in Heaven

STUDYQURAN:20:17/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:17/r4.speaker: al-Tustarī
STUDYQURAN:20:17/r4.claim: Al-Tustarī says Moses' claim about other uses will prove true when God makes the staff a means for several miracles, though Moses does not yet know this.
STUDYQURAN:20:17/r4.anchor: According to al-Tustarī, although Moses’ words I have other uses for it will become true in the future

STUDYQURAN:20:17/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:17/r5.speaker: al-Tustarī
STUDYQURAN:20:17/r5.claim: Al-Tustarī says God uses the moment to show Moses that even a prophet knows little beside God's knowledge.
STUDYQURAN:20:17/r5.anchor: This, al-Tustarī says, was God’s way of showing to Moses that even though he was to be a prophet

STUDYQURAN:20:17/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:17/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:20:17/r6.claim: The staff episode is also referenced in 27:10 and 28:31, and compared with Exodus 4:2.

TAB-FULL:v16p43/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p43/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p43/r1.claim: Moses leans on the staff and shakes dry trees so their leaves fall for his sheep to graze.
TAB-FULL:v16p43/r1.anchor: أضرب بها الشجر اليابس فيسقط ورقها وترعاه غنمي

TAB-FULL:v16p43/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p43/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p43/r2.claim: Hashsha means shaking branches until leaves fall; a rajaz verse uses the word for shaking a staff over sheep.
TAB-FULL:v16p43/r2.anchor: هش فلان الشجر يهش هشا: إذا اختبط ورق أغصانها فسقط ورقها

TAB-FULL:v16p43/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p43/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v16p43/r3.claim: Qatāda glosses the action as knocking or shaking the tree.
TAB-FULL:v16p43/r3.anchor: عن قتادة، في قوله: {وأهش بها على غنمي} [طه: 18] قال: أخبط بها الشجر

TAB-FULL:v16p43/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p43/r4.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v16p43/r4.claim: Qatāda also says Moses shook leaves from trees for his flock.
TAB-FULL:v16p43/r4.anchor: عن قتادة {وأهش بها على غنمي} [طه: 18] قال: كان نبي الله موسى صلى الله عليه وسلم يهش على غنمه ورق الشجر

TAB-FULL:v16p43/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p43/r5.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v16p43/r5.claim: Al-Suddī says Moses struck trees for the sheep so leaves fell.
TAB-FULL:v16p43/r5.anchor: عن السدي، {وأهش بها على غنمي} [طه: 18] يقول: أضرب بها الشجر للغنم، فيقع الورق

TAB-FULL:v16p43/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p43/r6.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v16p43/r6.claim: Ibn Zayd says Moses leaned on the staff while walking with the sheep and shook branches, including habala, to drop leaves.
TAB-FULL:v16p43/r6.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {هي عصاي أتوكأ عليها وأهش بها على غنمي} [طه: 18] قال: يتوكأ عليها حين يمشي مع الغنم، ويهش بها، يحرك الشجر حتى يسقط الورق الحبلة وغيرها

TAB-FULL:v16p43/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p43/r7.speaker: عكرمة
TAB-FULL:v16p43/r7.claim: ʿIkrima says Moses struck trees so leaves fell onto him or his sheep.
TAB-FULL:v16p43/r7.anchor: عن عكرمة، {وأهش بها على غنمي} [طه: 18] قال: أضرب بها الشجر، فيسقط من ورقها علي

TAB-FULL:v16p43/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p43/r8.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v16p43/r8.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says Moses struck the tree until leaves fell for his sheep to eat.
TAB-FULL:v16p43/r8.anchor: الضحاك، يقول في قوله {وأهش بها على غنمي} [طه: 18] يقول: أضرب بها الشجر حتى يسقط منه ما تأكل غنمي

TAB-FULL:v16p45/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p45/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p45/r1.claim: Maʾārib means needs or purposes, plural of maʾriba, derived from lā ariba lī, meaning I have no need; the ra has three dialectal vowelings.
TAB-FULL:v16p45/r1.anchor: وبنحو الذي قلنا في معنى المآرب، قال أهل التأويل

TAB-FULL:v16p45/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p45/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p45/r2.claim: Though maʾārib is plural, ukhrā is feminine singular, as with al-asmāʾ al-ḥusnā; the author refers to his earlier explanation of this agreement.
TAB-FULL:v16p45/r2.anchor: كما قيل: {له الأسماء الحسنى} [طه: 8] وقد بينت العلة في توجيه ذلك هنالك

TAB-FULL:v16p45/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p45/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v16p45/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the staff had other needs that Moses knew.
TAB-FULL:v16p45/r3.anchor: عن عكرمة، عن ابن عباس، في قوله: {ولي فيها مآرب أخرى} [طه: 18] قال: حوائج أخرى قد علمتها

TAB-FULL:v16p45/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p45/r4.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v16p45/r4.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد، {ولي فيها مآرب أخرى} [طه: 18] قال: حاجات

TAB-FULL:v16p45/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p45/r5.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v16p45/r5.claim: Mujāhid also glosses the phrase as needs and benefits.
TAB-FULL:v16p45/r5.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح، {ولي فيها مآرب أخرى} [طه: 18] قال: حاجات ومنافع

TAB-FULL:v16p45/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p45/r6.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v16p45/r6.claim: Al-Suddī says Moses used the staff to carry provisions and a water skin.
TAB-FULL:v16p45/r6.anchor: عن السدي، {ولي فيها مآرب أخرى} [طه: 18] يقول: حوائج أخرى أحمل عليها المزود والسقاء

TAB-FULL:v16p45/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p45/r7.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v16p45/r7.claim: Qatāda glosses the phrase as other needs and benefits.
TAB-FULL:v16p45/r7.anchor: عن قتادة، {ولي فيها مآرب أخرى} [طه: 18] قال: حوائج أخرى

TAB-FULL:v16p45/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p45/r8.speaker: وهب بن منبه
TAB-FULL:v16p45/r8.claim: Wahb ibn Munabbih says the staff served other benefits.
TAB-FULL:v16p45/r8.anchor: عن ابن إسحاق، عن وهب بن منبه، {ولي فيها مآرب أخرى} [طه: 18] أي منافع أخرى

TAB-FULL:v16p45/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p45/r9.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v16p45/r9.claim: Ibn Zayd says Moses had other needs for it besides those already mentioned.
TAB-FULL:v16p45/r9.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {ولي فيها مآرب أخرى} [طه: 18] قال: حوائج أخرى سوى ذلك

TAB-FULL:v16p45/r10.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p45/r10.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v16p45/r10.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk glosses the phrase as other needs.
TAB-FULL:v16p45/r10.anchor: الضحاك، يقول في قوله {مآرب أخرى} [طه: 18] قال: حاجات أخرى

SULAMI:v1p438#3/r5.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p438#3/r5.speaker: فارس
SULAMI:v1p438#3/r5.claim: Faris says Moses listed the staff's uses so he could return to them in conversation and delight in his Master's address and reproach.
SULAMI:v1p438#3/r5.anchor: قال فارس : ذكر كلما فيها من وجوه المنافع ليلا تكون له

SULAMI:v1p438#3/r6.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p438#3/r6.speaker: أبو بكر الوراق
SULAMI:v1p438#3/r6.claim: Abu Bakr al-Warraq says 'my staff' answers the question, while the following list of benefits gives thanks for God's gift of the staff.
SULAMI:v1p438#3/r6.anchor: قال أبو بكر الوراق : قوله : ﴿ عصاي ﴾ جواب والذي بعده

SULAMI:v1p438#3/r7.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p438#3/r7.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v1p438#3/r7.claim: Ibn Ata says Moses' possessive wording wrongly claimed ownership before God; after the staff became a serpent he renounced that claim in fear, and God reassured him to take it without harm.
SULAMI:v1p438#3/r7.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : في قوله : ﴿ عصاي ﴾ إضافة بالملك

SULAMI:v1p439/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p439/r1.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v1p439/r1.claim: Ibn Ata says the staff held hidden secrets that Moses did not know, which God disclosed to him as signs and gifts of grace.
SULAMI:v1p439/r1.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : سرائر مغيبة عني في العصا

SULAMI:v1p439/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p439/r2.speaker: جعفر
SULAMI:v1p439/r2.claim: Ja'far says the greatest of the staff's many benefits was that it occasioned God's address: What is that in your right hand, Moses?
SULAMI:v1p439/r2.anchor: قال جعفر : منافع شتى وأكبر منفعة لي فيها خطابك إياي

SULAMI:v1p439/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p439/r3.speaker: سهل
SULAMI:v1p439/r3.claim: Sahl says God showed Moses uses he had not known: the staff became a serpent, struck the rock to release water, and struck the sea to split it, demonstrating that even prophets' knowledge of the worlds is limited beside God's.
SULAMI:v1p439/r3.anchor: قال سهل : ذكر موسى من العصا مآرب ومنافع فأراه الله

TABATABAI:20:18-21/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:18-21/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:18-21/r2.claim: Alternatively, تلك points to the known staff but asks for its qualities, not its name; Moses understands this and lists its uses, as one may ask about an obvious thing to elicit description.
TABATABAI:20:18-21/r2.anchor: ويمكن أن تكون الإشارة بتلك إلى العصا لكن لا بداعي الاطلاع على اسمها وحقيقتها حتى يلغو الاستفهام

TABATABAI:20:18-21/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:18-21/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:18-21/r3.claim: Moses’s detailed description supports the reading that the question elicited the staff’s properties; the Qur’an uses comparable questions for obvious but momentous things in 6:78, 101:1–4, and 69:1–3.
TABATABAI:20:18-21/r3.anchor: ويؤيده ما في كلام موسى عليه السلام من الاطناب بذكر نعوت العصا وخواصها فإنه لما سمع السؤال عما في يمينه وهي عصا

TABATABAI:20:18-21/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:18-21/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:18-21/r4.claim: The staff is a feminine noun by Arabic convention; tawakkī or leaning on it means relying on it for support.
TABATABAI:20:18-21/r4.anchor: التوكي والاتكاء على العصا الاعتماد عليها

TABATABAI:20:18-21/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:18-21/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:18-21/r5.claim: Hashsh means striking or shaking tree foliage with a staff so that it falls for the sheep to eat.
TABATABAI:20:18-21/r5.anchor: والهش هو خبط ورق الشجرة وضربه بالعصا لتساقط على الغنم فيأكله

TABATABAI:20:18-21/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:18-21/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:18-21/r6.claim: Maʾārib is the plural of maʾriba, with the rāʾ read in any of three vowels, and means needs; his needs relate to the staff as a means of fulfilling them.
TABATABAI:20:18-21/r6.anchor: والمآرب جمع مأربة مثلثة الراء وهي الحاجة

TABATABAI:20:18-21/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:18-21/r7.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:20:18-21/r7.claim: One explanation says Moses elaborates because private conversation with the beloved is pleasurable; he first calls it his staff to introduce its general benefits.
TABATABAI:20:18-21/r7.anchor: قيل لأن المقام وهو مقام المناجاة والمسارة مع المحبوب يقتضي ذلك لأن مكالمة المحبوب لذيذة

TABATABAI:20:18-21/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:18-21/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:18-21/r8.claim: On al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī’s explanation of the question, the reply is not needless elaboration: Moses lists the uses and sums up other benefits in his final phrase.
TABATABAI:20:18-21/r8.anchor: وقد قدمنا في ذيل الآية السابقة وجها آخر لهذا الاستفهام وجوابه وليس الكلام عليه من باب الاطناب وخاصه بالنظر إلى جمعه سائر منافعها

TUSTARI:20:18/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:20:18/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:20:18/r1.claim: The staff first belonged to Adam, came from a Paradise myrtle, passed through the prophets to Shuʿayb, then Shuʿayb gave it to Moses with his daughter in marriage.
TUSTARI:20:18/r1.anchor: أول من ملك العصا آدم، وهي من آس الجنة، ثم انتقلت من نبي إلى نبي

TUSTARI:20:18/r2.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:20:18/r2.speaker: author
TUSTARI:20:18/r2.claim: Besides leaning on it and shaking leaves for his sheep, Moses used the staff to gather fodder, fend off animals, make shade, guard him at night, light darkness, mark prayer time, and produce fruit when he was hungry.
TUSTARI:20:18/r2.anchor: فكان موسى عليه السلام يتوكأ عليها، ويهش بها على غنمه

TUSTARI:20:18/r3.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:20:18/r3.speaker: author
TUSTARI:20:18/r3.claim: God meant further benefits hidden from Moses, including its turning into a serpent and its striking rock and sea; this shows that even prophets' knowledge falls short of God's knowledge of events.
TUSTARI:20:18/r3.anchor: فأراد الله تعالى مآرب ومنافع كانت خافية عليه، كانقلابها ثعبانا

FARRA:v2p176/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p176/r1.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p176/r1.claim: An unnamed poet’s لا نخفه means “we do not reveal it.”
FARRA:v2p176/r1.anchor: لا نخفه ... وإن تبعثوا الحرب لا نقعد يريد لا نظهره.

FARRA:v2p176/r5.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p176/r5.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p176/r5.claim: Moses strikes dry branches with his staff so leaves fall for his flock to eat.
FARRA:v2p176/r5.anchor: أضرب بها الشجر اليابس ليسقط ورقها فترعاه غنمه

FARRA:v2p176/r6.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p176/r6.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p176/r6.claim: مآرب is plural with أخرى as its adjective; أخر would also be possible, as in أيام أخر and الأسماء الحسنى.
FARRA:v2p176/r6.anchor: يعني حوائج جعل أخرى نعتا للمآرب وهي جمع. ولو قال: أخر، جاز

THALABI:v6p240/r14.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p240/r14.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p240/r14.claim: Moses leaned on the staff while walking or when tired, and used it when leaping.
THALABI:v6p240/r14.anchor: أتوكؤا اعتمد عليها إذا مشيت وإذا أعييت وعند الوثبة

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p278/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p278/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p278/r1.claim: Ahushshu bihā means striking leaves down with the staff.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p278/r1.anchor: وأهش بها على غنمي} أخبط بها الورق.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p278/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p278/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p278/r2.claim: Maʾārib means other needs or purposes; its singular is maʾriba or maʾraba.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p278/r2.anchor: ولي فيها مآرب أخرى} أي حوائج أخرى. واحدها: مأربة ومأربة.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p378/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p378/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p378/r1.claim: “It is my staff” answers the question about what Moses holds; the source says God then asked what he did with it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p378/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: {قال هي عصاي} جواب الاستفهام والسؤال عما في يده، قال وهب: (لما قال موسى: {هي عصاي}، قال الله تعالى: وما تصنع بها)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p378/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p378/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p378/r2.claim: The follow-up “I lean on it” answers what Moses does with the staff; identifying it had already sufficed to answer the first question.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p378/r2.anchor: ولا أحد أعلم منه بذلك، قال موسى: {أتوكأ عليها}؛ لأن # هذا جواب السؤال عما يصنع بها؟ والسؤال الأول يكفيه من الجواب قوله: {هي عصاي}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p378/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p378/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p378/r3.claim: Tawakkuʾ means leaning one’s weight on the staff while walking; the related form ittikaʾ derives from al-awtikaʾ.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p378/r3.anchor: ومعنى التوكؤ (¬1): التحامل على العصا في المشي، ومنه الاتكأ، أصله: الاوتكأ، والمعنى: أعتمد عليها إذا مشيت

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p378/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p378/r4.speaker: الأصمعي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p378/r4.claim: Al-Asmaʿi says hashsha means striking or shaking a tree so its leaves fall for the sheep.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p378/r4.anchor: قال الأصمعي: (هش يهش هشا: إذا خبط الشجر فألقاه لغنمه)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p378/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p378/r5.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p378/r5.claim: Al-Farra explains that Moses struck dry trees so their leaves fell for the sheep to graze.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p378/r5.anchor: قال الفراء: (أي أضرب بها الشجر اليابس ليسقط ورقه فترعاه الغنم)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p378/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p378/r6.speaker: الراجز
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p378/r6.claim: A rajaz line uses ahush with a staff for shaking foliage from arak and bashsham trees for sheep.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p378/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p378/r7.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p378/r7.claim: Al-Zajjaj derives the word from making something soft and pliable; fallen foliage becomes easy for sheep to eat.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p378/r7.anchor: قال الزجاج: (واشتقاقه من أني أحيل الشيء إلى الهشاشة والإمكان)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p378/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p378/r8.speaker: عكرمة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p378/r8.claim: Ikrima glosses the action as beating the tree so its leaves fall onto Moses’ flock.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p378/r8.anchor: قال عكرمة: (يقال: أضرب الشجر فيتساقط الورق على غنمي)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p380/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p380/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p380/r1.claim: Maʾārib means needs; the singular maʾriba is reported with fatḥa or ḍamma on the rāʾ by the linguists.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p380/r1.anchor: المآرب: الحوائج، واحدتها مأربة بفتح الراء وضمها، حكاهما جميع أهل اللغة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p380/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p380/r2.speaker: ابن الأعرابي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p380/r2.claim: Ibn al-Aʿrabi also records the singular maʾriba with kasra on the rāʾ.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p380/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p380/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p380/r3.claim: The proverb “a need, not hospitality” and the forms al-arab and al-irba share the same root, as in “those without desire” at 24:31.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p380/r3.anchor: ومنه المثل: مأربة لا حفاوة (¬4). وكذلك الأرب والإربة ومنه قوله تعالى: {غير أولي الإربة من الرجال}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p380/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p380/r4.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p380/r4.claim: Al-Zajjaj explains the feminine singular ukhrā despite plural maʾārib because the latter denotes a collective of needs; a similar construction occurs at 20:8.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p380/r4.anchor: وقوله تعالى: {أخرى} جاء على لفظ صيغه الواحدة؛ لأن مأرب في معنى جماعة، فكأنه جماعة من الحاجات أخرى. وقاله الزجاج

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p380/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p380/r5.speaker: مجاهد وسفيان والمفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p380/r5.claim: Mujahid, Sufyan, and the commentators say Moses means that he has other needs for the staff.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p380/r5.anchor: قال مجاهد، وسفيان والمفسرون: (ولي فيها حاجات أخرى)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p380/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p380/r6.speaker: عطاء وقتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p380/r6.claim: ʿAta and Qatada gloss the staff’s other uses as additional benefits.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p380/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p380/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p380/r7.claim: In the report through ʿAta, Ibn Abbas lists using the staff to lengthen a short well rope, make shade, and kill ground vermin.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p380/r7.anchor: فقال ابن عباس في رواية عطاء: (إذا أتيت إلى بئر فقصر الرشا، وصلته بالعصا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p380/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p380/r8.speaker: وهب
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p380/r8.claim: Wahb describes a forked, hooked staff for bending or breaking branches, carrying Moses’ gear, and fighting predators threatening his sheep.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p380/r8.anchor: وقال وهب: (كان لها شعبتان ومحجن (¬2) تحت الشعبتين، فإذا طال الغصن حناه بالمحجن، وإذا أراد كسره لواه بالشعبتين،

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:15-18/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:15-18/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:15-18/r5.claim: Moses leans on his staff when walking or tired.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:15-18/r5.anchor: { قال هي عصاي أتوكؤا عليها } أتحامل عليها عند المشي والإعياء

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:15-18/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:15-18/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:15-18/r6.claim: He uses it to knock leaves from trees for his sheep.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:15-18/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:15-18/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:15-18/r7.claim: The staff has other uses besides leaning on it and knocking down leaves.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:15-18/r7.anchor: { بها على غنمي ولى فيها مآرب أخرى } حاجات أخرى سوى التوكؤ والهش.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p256/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p256/r3.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p256/r3.claim: Qatadah says Moses beat leaves down from trees with the staff for his sheep.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p256/r3.anchor: قال قتادة: كان يهش بها على غنمه ورق الشجر، أي يخبط بها ورق الشجر لغنمه

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p256/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p256/r4.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p256/r4.anchor: سعيد، عن قتادة قال: المآرب، الحوائج

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p256/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p256/r5.speaker: يحيى
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p256/r5.claim: Yahya says he has been told that one of Moses’s other uses for the staff was to shade himself.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p256/r5.anchor: قال يحيى: بلغني أن من تلك الحوائج الأخرى أنه كان يستظل بها

MAJAZ:v2p17/r1.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p17/r1.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p17/r1.claim: Ahushsh means striking branches with the staff so leaves fall for the sheep to eat; the poem explicitly uses ahushshu for this.
MAJAZ:v2p17/r1.anchor: وأهش بها على غنمي» (18) أي أختبط بها فأضرب بها الأغصان ليسقط ورقها على غنمى فتأكله، قال:

MAJAZ:v2p17/r2.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p17/r2.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p17/r2.claim: The singular of maʾārib is maʾriba or maʾraba, with the rāʾ either fatḥa or ḍamma; it means needs, from ‘I have no need of it.’
MAJAZ:v2p17/r2.anchor: مآرب أخرى» (18) واحدتها مأربة ومأربة، الراء مفتوحة ويضمها قوم، ومعناها حوائج وهى من قولهم: لا أرب لى فيها

NAHHAS:v3p35/r15.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p35/r15.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p35/r15.claim: The source records two spoken forms, أهش and أهش, without naming a reader or giving a gloss.
NAHHAS:v3p35/r15.anchor: لا يجوز أن توصل الأسماء المبهمة ويقال ( أهش ) و أهش

ITQAN:v2p574/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p574/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p574/r2.claim: Moses gives more than the requested identification of the staff, adding its uses because he delights in being addressed by God.
ITQAN:v2p574/r2.anchor: وقول موسى ﴿ هي عصاي أتوكأ عليها وأهش بها على غنمي ﴾ في جواب ﴿ وما تلك بيمينك يا موسى ﴾ زاد في الجواب استلذاذا بخطاب الله تعالى

TABRISI:20:17-36/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:17-36/r1.speaker: ابن عامر
TABRISI:20:17-36/r1.claim: Ibn Amir reads أشدد with hamza of قطع and an open hamza, and أشركه with a damma; the other readers use hamzat al-wasl and fatḥ.
TABRISI:20:17-36/r1.anchor: قرأ ابن عامر أشدد بقطع الهمزة وفتحها وأشركه بضمها

TABRISI:20:17-36/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:17-36/r2.speaker: عكرمة وأبو البرهسم
TABRISI:20:17-36/r2.claim: In noncanonical readings, Ikrima has وأهس with sin, while Abu al-Barhasm has وأهش with a kasra under the ه.
TABRISI:20:17-36/r2.anchor: وفي الشواذ قراءة عكرمة وأهس بالسين وقراءة أبي البرهسم وأهش بكسر الهاء

TABRISI:20:17-36/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:17-36/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:17-36/r3.claim: Ibn Amir's reading makes أشدد indicative, while the others make it a supplication; the damma in أشركه is very weak because Moses cannot himself make Aaron a prophet, so fatḥ as a prayer is fitting.
TABRISI:20:17-36/r3.anchor: الوجه في قراءة أبي عامر أنه جعله خبرا وسائر القراء جعلوه دعاء

TABRISI:20:17-36/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:17-36/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:17-36/r4.claim: The kasra in أهش may represent the damma form, meaning to strike fodder for the sheep; Arabic also has paired intransitive and transitive forms like يهر ويهره and يشد ويشده.
TABRISI:20:17-36/r4.anchor: أراد أهش بضم الهاء أي أكسر الكلاء بها للغنم

TABRISI:20:17-36/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:17-36/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:17-36/r5.claim: أهس means to drive; although one would expect أهس بها غنمي, the preposition عليها follows the sense of driving them toward and along with her.
TABRISI:20:17-36/r5.anchor: وأما أهس بالسين فمعناه أسوق وكان ينبغي أن يقول أهس بها غنمي

TABRISI:20:17-36/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:17-36/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:17-36/r6.claim: التوكؤ and الاتكاء mean the same; الهش is beating tree leaves down, and مآرب means needs, with مأربة having three possible vowelings.
TABRISI:20:17-36/r6.anchor: التوكؤ والاتكاء بمعنى مثل التوقي والاتقاء والهش ضرب ورق الشجر

TABRISI:20:17-36/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:17-36/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:17-36/r7.claim: السيرة and الطريقة are synonyms and denote a thing's passage along a direction.
TABRISI:20:17-36/r7.anchor: والسيرة والطريقة من النظائر ومعناه مرور الشيء في جهة

TABRISI:20:17-36/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:17-36/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:17-36/r8.claim: جناح derives from جنوح, inclination in flight; a person's arm is his wing because it lets the hand incline as its owner wishes. Another explanation refers to the flank because of the ribs' bend.
TABRISI:20:17-36/r8.anchor: وأصل الجناح من الجنوح وهو الميل لأن الطائر يميل به في طيرانه

TABRISI:20:17-36/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:17-36/r9.speaker: الراجز
TABRISI:20:17-36/r9.claim: A rajaz poet uses الجناح in a line about drawing something to the chest and side.

TABRISI:20:17-36/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:17-36/r10.speaker: أبو عبيدة
TABRISI:20:17-36/r10.claim: Abu Ubayda says the two wings mean the two sides.

TABRISI:20:17-36#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:17-36#2/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:17-36#2/r5.claim: Moses says he leans on his staff when walking; التوكؤ is putting one's weight on the staff while walking.
TABRISI:20:17-36#2/r5.anchor: أي أعتمد عليها إذا مشيت والتوكؤ التحامل على العصا

TABRISI:20:17-36#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:17-36#2/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:17-36#2/r6.claim: He strikes leaves from trees with the staff so that his sheep can eat them.
TABRISI:20:17-36#2/r6.anchor: أي وأخبط بها ورق الشجر لترعاه غنمي

TABRISI:20:17-36#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:17-36#2/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:17-36#2/r7.claim: Moses means other needs; he names the staff's regular use and alludes to its incidental uses.
TABRISI:20:17-36#2/r7.anchor: أي حاجات أخرى فنص على اللازم وكنى عن العارض

TABRISI:20:17-36#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:17-36#2/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:20:17-36#2/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas lists the staff's other uses: carrying provisions; producing water when planted in the ground and food when striking it; driving off predators; fighting enemies; extending into a bucket for drawing water; shining at night; speaking and keeping Moses company; and bending high branches with its crook.
TABRISI:20:17-36#2/r8.anchor: قال ابن عباس: كان يحمل عليها زاده ويركزها

BURHAN:v4p44/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p44/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p44/r7.claim: Moses expanded his answer about the object in his hand because he sensed that a great event involving the staff was coming and wanted to describe its ordinary uses first.
BURHAN:v4p44/r7.anchor: ومثال الزيادة في الجواب قوله تعالى

BIQAI-FULL:v5p16/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p16/r1.speaker: مالك
BIQAI-FULL:v5p16/r1.claim: Ibn Kathīr transmits from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. al-Qāsim that Mālik defines hashing as shaking leaves and fruit from a branch with a hooked staff without breaking or beating it.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p16/r1.anchor: قال عبد الرحمن بن القاسم عن الإمام مالك

BIQAI-FULL:v5p16/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p16/r2.speaker: ميمون بن مهران
BIQAI-FULL:v5p16/r2.claim: Maymūn b. Mihrān gives the same explanation of gently shaking foliage from branches.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p16/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p16/r3.speaker: أبو حيان
BIQAI-FULL:v5p16/r3.claim: Abū Ḥayyān says the root sense of this word is softness, as in describing a man as هش.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p16/r3.anchor: وقال أبو حيان : والأصل في هذه المادة الرخاوة

BIQAI-FULL:v5p16/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p16/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p16/r4.claim: Moses cuts short his account out of respect for the King and eagerness to hear God speak, recalling the maxim against overfamiliarity on a royal carpet.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p16/r4.anchor: خاف التطويل على الملك فقطع على نفسه ما هو فيه من لذة المخاطبة

BIQAI-FULL:v5p16/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p16/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p16/r5.claim: Maʾārib means needs or benefits, which perceptive people can understand.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p16/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p16/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p16/r6.claim: Because maʾārib is a nonrational broken plural, it takes the feminine singular modifier أخرى; Moses leaves the particular uses unspecified.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p16/r6.anchor: كان الأنسب معاملته معاملة الواحدة المؤنثة

JISHUMI:v6p4646/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4646/r1.speaker: عكرمة
JISHUMI:v6p4646/r1.claim: The common reading has أهش with shin; Ikrima read it with sin, which the author calls unfamiliar. Al-Nadr says Arabs interchange the sounds, and some connect it with a sheep-herding call.
JISHUMI:v6p4646/r1.anchor: القراءة الظاهرة: وأهش بالشين، وعن عكرمة بالسين؛ لكنه ليس بالمعروف. وسئل النضر بن شميل عنه

JISHUMI:v6p4646/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4646/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4646/r2.claim: Yamīn first means the known bodily right hand, then by extension strength and an oath.
JISHUMI:v6p4646/r2.anchor: اليمين: الجارحة المعروفة، وهو الأصل، ثم يستعمل في القوة، وهو في القسم

JISHUMI:v6p4646/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4646/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4646/r3.claim: Tawakkuʾ and ittikāʾ both mean leaning; their verb forms are tafaʿʿala and iftaʿala respectively.
JISHUMI:v6p4646/r3.anchor: والتوكؤ والاتكاء واحد، مثل التوقي والاتقاء، وبناء توكأت: تفعلت، وبناء اتكأت: افتعلت

JISHUMI:v6p4646/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4646/r4.speaker: قطرب
JISHUMI:v6p4646/r4.claim: Qutrub glosses hashsh as striking tree leaves so they fall; the Rajaz verse uses أهش for beating leaves for sheep.
JISHUMI:v6p4646/r4.anchor: والهمش: ضرب ورق الشجر ليتساقط، عن قطرب، هش يهش هشا، قال الراجز: أهش بالعصا على أغنامي

JISHUMI:v6p4646/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4646/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4646/r5.claim: Maʾārib means needs or purposes, from irb; its singular maʾraba has three vowel variants, as Ali ibn Isa notes.
JISHUMI:v6p4646/r5.anchor: والمآرب: الحوائج، والأصل: الإرب، يقال: ما في هذا إرب، والمآرب في واحده ثلاث لغات

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p724/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p724/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p724/r3.claim: Moses used his staff to tend his sheep, a merciful, opposite function that did not suit the word minsaʾa.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p724/r3.anchor: ليهشّ بها على غنمه وبها رحمة بالحيوان وعكس الأولى ولا يناسب استخدام كلمة منسأة
